title: Quantum Entanglement Computation Adaptive Quantum Entanglement Arrangement Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental resource in quantum computing, enabling functionalities beyond classical computation. However, maintaining entanglement coherence – the ability to sustain entanglement across time – is a significant challenge in quantum computing. This paper proposes a novel self-adaptive quantum entanglement arrangement algorithm, designed to maximize computational efficiency and stability. The algorithm dynamically adjusts the entanglement strength, direction, and connections between qubits based on the evolving quantum system state. We present a conceptual framework and preliminary results demonstrating this approach's potential to overcome limitations of traditional entanglement management techniques. The core mechanism focuses on implementing a "quantum entanglement intelligence" that continuously monitors and responds to changes in the quantum system, ensuring optimal entanglement distribution and minimizing decoherence. This advancement promises to unlock new capabilities within quantum computation, fostering a "quantum multi-agent" system.

title: Explainable AI for Federated Learning – Attribution of Contributions
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without direct data sharing. However, the inherent lack of transparency in FL raises concerns about trust, fairness, and model reliability. This paper explores the critical need for explainable AI (XAI) techniques within the FL paradigm, specifically focusing on attributing contributions from individual participants to the global model. We propose a novel framework for tracing the influence of local model updates, quantifying the impact of each participant's contribution on the global model's parameters. Our methodology leverages gradient analysis and differential privacy considerations to provide a granular understanding of the learning process. The core claim is that understanding these contributions is essential for fostering trust and ensuring fairness in FL deployments. The developed attribution methods provide insights into the learning dynamics, allowing for the identification of potential biases or anomalous behavior. This work aims to establish a foundation for more robust and accountable FL systems.

title: Adaptive Kernel Learning for Anomaly Detection
abstract: This paper presents a novel adaptive kernel learning algorithm designed for anomaly detection. Traditional kernel methods, while effective, often suffer from computational bottlenecks, particularly when dealing with non-stationary data. This work addresses this limitation by introducing a Bayesian-driven approach that dynamically adjusts the kernel function to better capture the underlying data distribution. The core idea is to continuously monitor the kernel's performance and adapt its parameters, thereby optimizing the detection of anomalies. The algorithm leverages a kernel learning framework to estimate the data distribution and uses this estimate to refine the kernel function. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through a theoretical analysis and a conceptual outline of its implementation. The key contributions of this work are the integration of Bayesian principles with kernel learning for anomaly detection and the proposed mechanism for adaptive kernel parameter tuning. The goal is to create a robust and computationally efficient anomaly detection system that can handle evolving data environments.

abstract: This paper investigates the construction of cognitive graphs using multimodal neural networks. title: Dynamically Weighted Bayesian Networks for Anomaly Detection
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to anomaly detection using Dynamically Weighted Bayesian Networks (DWBNs). Traditional Bayesian Networks (BNs) struggle with evolving anomalies due to their static structure. We introduce a framework where the edge weights within a BN are continuously updated based on observed data patterns. This dynamic adjustment allows the DWBN to adapt to changes in the system and, consequently, more accurately identify anomalous events. The core claim is that static BNs are inherently inadequate for this task. The methodology focuses on constructing a BN and implementing a weighting mechanism that responds to data shifts. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a theoretical analysis and outline a practical implementation strategy. The key innovation lies in the real-time adaptability of the network, offering a significantly improved detection capability compared to static BN models.

title: Clustering Netflix Play Store Reviews Using K-Means and Hierarchical Algorithms to Identify User Experience Patterns
abstract: User reviews posted on Google Play Store contain rich, unstructured evidence of how subscribers experience a streaming platform, complementing structured behavioral or transactional data. This study applies unsupervised text clustering to a Kaggle dataset of 154,532 Netflix Play Store reviews. A random sample of 5,000 reviews with non-null text was cleaned, lemmatized, and represented as a Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) matrix restricted to 1,000 unigrams (min_df=5, max_df=0.8). KMeans and agglomerative hierarchical clustering with Ward linkage were fitted at k=3, a value supported by the elbow curve, the dendrogram, and a full k=2-10 metric sweep. Ward clustering achieved a Silhouette Score of 0.0297 and a Davies-Bouldin Index (DBI) of 1.3049, outperforming KMeans (0.0229 and 5.9106, respectively). Profiling the KMeans clusters by top TF-IDF terms revealed three interpretable segments: a technical/account-issue segment (71.1% of reviews, mean rating 2.35), a concise highlysatisfied segment (2.8%, mean rating 4.51), and a contentsatisfaction segment (26.1%, mean rating 4.07). A chi-square test confirmed a statistically significant association between cluster membership and star rating (χ²=1085.33, p<0.001). A supplementary experiment using TruncatedSVD (Latent Semantic Analysis, 50 components, 30.5% variance explained) improved Ward's Silhouette Score to 0.3526 and DBI to 0.7914, indicating that the weak raw-TF-IDF separation is largely a dimensionality artifact rather than an absence of underlying structure. Keywords: text clustering, K-Means, hierarchical clustering, TF-IDF, latent semantic analysis, Netflix, Google Play Store reviews, user experience, opinion mining

title: A Trustworthy Watermarking Framework for LLM-Generated Food Safety Content
abstract: Large language models are transforming many industries with their text generation abilities. However, their outputs can be easily tampered with, creating serious risks in critical areas such as food safety reporting. To protect the integrity and traceability of AI-generated content, this paper introduces ToSS (Token Oriented Repartitioning and Strategic Selection), a reliable authentication method using adaptive dual watermarking. The key innovation of ToSS is its dual watermark encoding approach that divides vocabulary tokens into black and white sublists, enabling precise bit-level embedding of traceability information. Additionally, an entropy adaptive mechanism dynamically selects text regions with high prediction uncertainty for watermark insertion, maintaining text fluency and factual accuracy while ensuring reliable traceability. Experiments on multiple datasets, including food domain texts, demonstrate that ToSS achieves leading performance in both watermark capacity and decoding accuracy.

title: Algorithmic Complexity Metrics for Biological Systems
abstract: This paper explores the development of novel algorithmic complexity metrics specifically tailored for analyzing the computational demands of biological systems, including protein folding, gene regulation, and cellular signaling pathways. Traditional complexity measures often lack the nuanced understanding required to effectively model and analyze these systems. This work proposes a new set of metrics focusing on both the quantity and efficiency of operations, aiming to provide a more robust and insightful framework for understanding the computational bottlenecks inherent in biological processes. We introduce a new metric, the "Operational Efficiency Score" (OES), which incorporates both computational cost and the degree of resource utilization, offering a more comprehensive assessment of algorithmic complexity. The paper details the design and validation of the OES, emphasizing its potential to improve our understanding of biological computational challenges and guide the development of more efficient algorithms.

abstract: This paper investigates the application of dynamic topology quantum algorithms to the verification of quantum algorithms and the analysis of their influence on quantum geometry. abstract: This paper presents Adaptive Complexity Scaling (ACS), a novel method for automatically scaling the complexity of computational models based on input data. This allows the system to effectively handle diverse datasets without requiring explicit, fixed complexity settings. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of ACS in various scenarios, highlighting its potential for accelerating model development and improving performance.

The proposed mechanism leverages a self-learning algorithm to optimize the entanglement distribution and entanglement duration, thereby unlocking the potential of quantum computing. This research addresses a critical limitation in current quantum computing architectures – the reliance on manual parameter adjustment – and paves the way for more efficient and scalable quantum algorithms.

title: Algorithmic Self-Repair via Genetic Programming and Simulation
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to software self-repair, leveraging the power of genetic programming (GP) and simulated environments. The core idea is to evolve a population of repair algorithms, represented as genetic programs, within a controlled simulation, allowing them to autonomously identify and rectify faults within a target software system. Unlike traditional debugging methods which are reactive and require human intervention, this system offers a proactive, evolutionary strategy. The system's efficacy relies on the simulated environment accurately mirroring the target system's complexity and potential vulnerabilities. title: Dynamic Programming for Quantum Algorithm Design
abstract: The design of efficient quantum algorithms frequently relies on intuitive heuristics and extensive trial-and-error processes. This research proposes a novel dynamic programming (DP) framework to systematically explore the vast space of potential quantum circuits, aiming to optimize both circuit structure and gate sequences based on computational cost and expected fidelity. The framework utilizes a bottom-up approach, building solutions from smaller subproblems, leveraging previously computed results to avoid redundant calculations. This approach contrasts with traditional, often ad-hoc, methods for quantum algorithm design. The core contribution lies in formally applying dynamic programming to this problem, providing a structured methodology for algorithm development that can potentially reduce the reliance on guesswork and accelerate the discovery of optimal quantum solutions. The presented framework incorporates key elements such as state representation, transition functions, and optimal substructure assumptions to guarantee efficiency and accuracy. This paper outlines the framework, its underlying principles, and potential applications within the broader field of quantum algorithm design.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Hybrid Programming with Adaptive Modularization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to neuro-symbolic hybrid programming centered around adaptive modularization. The core idea is to enable neural networks to dynamically adjust their internal structure – specifically, the selection and combination of neural symbolic modules – based on the input data and the task objective. This contrasts with traditional methods that rely on pre-defined, fixed architectures, limiting their adaptability and generalization capabilities. We propose a mechanism where the neural network learns to autonomously choose and integrate different neural symbolic and neural network modules, leading to more efficient and robust intelligent agents. The key contribution lies in the ability to create a system that can dynamically adapt to diverse environments and tasks, ultimately improving both the learning efficiency and the overall performance of the agent. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through a theoretical framework and a proposed algorithmic design, outlining the fundamental principles for realizing a truly adaptive neuro-symbolic hybrid system.

title: Dynamic Topology Quantum State Generation Model
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic topology quantum state generation model, designed to produce quantum states with tailored properties through adaptive parameter adjustments. Traditional quantum state generation methods often rely on predefined algorithms, limiting the design flexibility of quantum states. We introduce a system that dynamically modifies the topology of a quantum system, generating unique states based on these modifications. This model offers a pathway to explore novel quantum phenomena and provides a foundation for advanced quantum computations. The core mechanism centers around the iterative adjustment of topology parameters to achieve desired quantum characteristics. We explore the potential of this approach to unlock new possibilities in quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Geometry and the Fusion of Higher-Order Matrices
abstract: Quantum geometry, a theoretical framework rooted in the principles of quantum mechanics, offers a unique perspective on geometric properties and their relationships. This paper investigates the potential integration of quantum geometry with higher-order matrix operations, aiming to enhance computational precision and potentially uncover novel geometric phenomena. We explore how quantum geometric transformations can be leveraged to optimize matrix calculations, presenting a novel approach through a carefully designed combination of these two fields. The study will focus on the inherent advantages offered by quantum geometry in manipulating space and transformation, and how this can be translated into enhanced matrix operations. The paper will detail a preliminary conceptual model and discuss potential avenues for future research and validation.

title: Based on Quantum Entanglement, Geometric Reasoning
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize geometric reasoning. We propose a novel mechanism utilizing entangled quantum particles to achieve more precise geometric transformations and to potentially uncover new geometric principles. The core of our investigation lies in designing a quantum entanglement protocol that allows for the transfer and manipulation of geometric information across multiple entangled states. This approach offers a fundamentally different pathway compared to traditional geometric modeling, leveraging the unique properties of entanglement to achieve unprecedented accuracy and insight. The research aims to demonstrate the feasibility of this concept through theoretical analysis and potential experimental exploration. We will discuss the challenges and opportunities associated with implementing this method, emphasizing the role of entanglement in achieving a higher level of geometric understanding.

title: Generative Adversarial Networks for Robotic Skill Discovery
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to robotic skill discovery utilizing Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). The core idea is to leverage a competitive learning framework where a generator proposes robotic actions, and a discriminator assesses the effectiveness of those actions in performing a given task. Unlike traditional trial-and-error methods, this approach utilizes a generative model to explore the skill space, potentially uncovering previously unseen and more efficient solutions. The presented framework aims to automate the process of skill discovery, reducing the need for manually designed skill sets and accelerating the development of robots capable of complex tasks. The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated through a theoretical analysis and conceptual design, focusing on the architecture and training dynamics of the proposed GAN. Key metrics for evaluating the performance of the generator and discriminator are outlined. Further research directions involving specific robotic platforms and task environments are suggested.

title: Decentralized Federated Learning with Blockchain-Based Incentive Mechanisms
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without directly exchanging data. However, a key challenge in the widespread adoption of FL is the incentive problem: motivating participants to contribute their valuable data and computational resources. This paper proposes a novel decentralized federated learning system incorporating a blockchain-based incentive mechanism. The system leverages smart contracts on a blockchain to reward participants based on their contributions, enhancing the scalability, robustness, and trust of the FL process. The core claim is that incentivizing participation is a significant hurdle in FL, and this work presents a mechanism to address this. We detail the design of the system, focusing on the blockchain architecture, the smart contract implementation for reward distribution, and the overall protocol for federated learning. The system aims to create a self-regulating and trustworthy FL environment where participants are actively encouraged to contribute, ultimately leading to more robust and efficient model training.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Program Synthesis with Temporal Reasoning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to program synthesis that integrates neural networks with symbolic programming and, crucially, incorporates temporal reasoning. The core idea is to construct programs automatically by leveraging the pattern recognition abilities of neural networks alongside the logical precision of symbolic representations. The system learns from a set of examples to construct initial symbolic representations of the problem. A neural network then refines these representations, ultimately generating executable code. A key advancement lies in the incorporation of temporal dependencies – essential for many real-world problems – which are modeled and handled within the symbolic reasoning process. This allows the synthesized programs to not only solve the problem correctly but also to execute in a temporally consistent manner. The system demonstrates the potential to create more sophisticated and adaptable software solutions compared to traditional approaches.

title: Cognitive Graph Embeddings for Knowledge Graph Reasoning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to knowledge graph (KG) reasoning utilizing cognitive graph embeddings. Traditional graph embeddings, such as node2vec and Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs), primarily focus on capturing structural relationships between nodes, often overlooking the cognitive processes involved in human understanding and reasoning within a KG. Our method addresses this limitation by integrating cognitive science principles into the embedding learning process. We develop an algorithm that explicitly models concepts, relationships, and inference rules, aiming to generate embeddings that reflect the underlying cognitive structure of the KG. This approach allows for more nuanced and accurate reasoning tasks compared to conventional graph embeddings. We demonstrate the potential of this method through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, outlining a framework for future research and development. The core contribution lies in bridging the gap between graph representation learning and cognitive modeling, leading to more interpretable and effective KG reasoning systems.

title: Quantum Topological Logic Devices: A Novel Approach to Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper proposes a novel architecture for quantum computing based on topological crystalline transistors protected by topological principles. The core concept leverages non-Abelian anyons to implement a topological quantum error correction code, offering a pathway to robust quantum computation resistant to local disturbances. We detail the theoretical framework, focusing on the design principles and mathematical formalism underlying this approach. The architecture utilizes specially engineered topological crystals to confine and manipulate anyons, enabling reliable quantum operations. We present a rigorous analysis of the error correction mechanisms, demonstrating the potential for significantly improved fault tolerance compared to conventional qubit designs. Key aspects include the encoding scheme using braiding operations of anyons, the topological redundancy for error detection and correction, and the resulting improved qubit fidelity. The proposed design represents a significant step towards practical, scalable quantum computers capable of enduring the inherent challenges of quantum decoherence. The presented model highlights the crucial role of topological protection in realizing a stable and reliable quantum computing platform. Our focus is on the theoretical development and the underlying mathematical structure of this approach, laying the groundwork for future experimental investigations.

title: Generative Adversarial Networks for Reinforcement Learning Reward Shaping
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) agents often struggle with sparse or delayed reward signals, leading to poor sample efficiency and difficulty in exploration. Reward shaping, the process of designing intermediate rewards to guide the agent, has proven effective but typically requires significant domain expertise and careful tuning. This paper proposes a novel approach utilizing Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to automatically learn reward functions for RL agents. The core idea is to train a GAN to generate reward signals that effectively shape the agent's behavior, allowing it to learn from potentially sparse or delayed rewards. We formulate the problem as a two-player game, where a generator network produces reward signals and a discriminator network assesses the quality of these signals in guiding the RL agent. Our experiments demonstrate that GAN-based reward shaping significantly improves the sample efficiency and exploration capabilities of RL agents compared to traditional reward shaping methods or standard RL without reward shaping. The key contribution lies in the automated and data-driven generation of reward functions, removing the need for manual design and potentially unlocking the potential of complex and challenging RL environments.

title: Delete Names Five Operations: Erasure Semantics for Derived Agent Memory, and Why a State-Level Definition Cannot Be the Auditable One
abstract: (c) 2026 Pranay Mahendrakar. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. Persistent memory has become a standard component of language-model agents, and with it a standard assumption: that where a fact lives in a retrievable store rather than in weights, erasing it is a solved problem, because a store supports deletion and weights do not. Agent memory does not hold the records that assumption presumes. It holds derivations - extracted facts, consolidated summaries, reflections, learned procedures, and edits made to earlier entries because a later one arrived - and deleting a source does not remove what was derived from it. This paper separates the operations that the single word delete is used for in this literature: removing the stored item, withdrawing everything derived from it, barring it from supporting an outgoing claim, making the fact non-inferable from what remains, and restoring the store to the state that would have obtained had the item never been written. Three systems published in 2026 supply a semantics for one of these each, and they are not the same semantics. The paper argues that the second is the database view-deletion problem, which has a known structure - no unique source update, and two inequivalent minimality objectives - that the agent-memory literature is rediscovering without the vocabulary; that the fourth is not a property of a record at all, and that deletion is itself an inference signal; and that the fifth is not defined for LLM-mediated consolidation, because the same trajectories are reported to yield different memories under different update schedules. The parametric unlearning literature reached the parallel conclusion in 2021, that only an algorithmic-level definition is auditable. What is not known is stated flatly: no work located for this paper reports what fraction of a production memory store's entries carry a recoverable derivation link to their sources. Six measurements are specified. The literature search, drafting and citation verification for this paper were carried out with AI assistance under the author's direction. Every citation was machine-verified against the arXiv API and Crossref before inclusion, and every quantitative claim was read back against the cited source's own abstract or, where a claim is drawn from a paper's body, against the located passage. The author is responsible for the final text and for all claims made in it.

title: Geometric Distributional Control: Learning Progress with Partial Structural Knowledge
abstract: Real-time control often sits between two limiting regimes. Predictive optimization and model-based control are powerful when dynamics, parameters, objectives, and online planning models are specified; reinforcement learning can relax this requirement, but must infer long-horizon value signals from sequential data and interaction, making training slow, high-variance, and hard to scale in large action spaces. This middle regime is common in systems including autonomous driving, warehouse robotics, traffic control, and delivery drones: partial geometry, physics, rules, or constraints are known, yet the local direction of task progress remains uncertain. Geometric Distributional Control (GDC) is designed for this partial-knowledge setting. It factorizes control into feasibility and progress: known geometry, rules, constraints, and response maps define an executable scaffold, while progress-weighted feasible data learns the missing directional signal on that scaffold. The learned score acts as a Bellman-like local value-gradient, selecting actions that make progress without requiring global Bellman recursion, a fully specified planner, or a black-box policy that absorbs both feasibility and preference. This knowledge can be lightweight and partial, such as simple dynamics, safety filters, local maps, constraint projectors, or lower-level response maps; it need not encode full dynamics or a long-horizon objective. Offline, GDC fits a progress-tilted distribution from short known-feasible snippets with weak signed progress certificates. Online, its score is projected through the scaffold and applied in receding-horizon feedback. We prove that this score descends a data-induced soft progress value and validate GDC on structured multilevel optimization and SUMO route-progress driving, where it improves over known-only solvers and learning baselines while preserving scaffold-enforced feasibility.

title: Thinking-Trace Analysis: Methodology for Surfacing Operational Improvements and Behavioral-Contract Candidates from Agent Planning Text
abstract: This paper records a methodology for analyzing AI agent thinking traces: the extended planning text an agent produces before and during task execution. The methodology uses a two-pass structure. The first pass is a piece-by-piece temporal pass that extracts operational improvements, behavioral-contract candidates, vocabulary coinages, and efficiency patterns per trace segment. The second is a structural synthesis pass that ranks improvements by leverage and attributes overhead to either the system (form and protocol gaps) or the agent (judgment patterns). The central analytical question is whether observed overhead is structural or behavioral, because the distinction determines the appropriate remediation. The methodology is demonstrated on one trace from an experimental inquest design task. Limitations include single-trace calibration, analyst-dependent segmentation, and invisibility of absent reasoning.

title: Co-Creative Adaptation in Long-Term Naturalistic Dialogue with ChatGPT: Distinguishing User Adaptation from Sycophancy
abstract: Conversational AI systems adapt their responses to users, which supports personalization and practical assistance. At the same time, such adaptation has been problematized as sycophancy: excessive agreement with or deference to a user's views. Treating every response that appears to adapt to a user as sycophancy, however, makes it difficult to capture interactions in which an AI reorganizes material around the user's aims and interests while leaving differences in judgment intact, and the human continues to evaluate, revise, and ask follow-up questions. This study is an exploratory, descriptive qualitative observational study of naturalistic dialogue sustained by a single user in the course of real-world ChatGPT use. Five cases were purposively selected from research, academic writing, text editing, creative work, and everyday interaction to provide detailed descriptions of multi-turn sequences relevant to the research question. The analysis traced human input, AI responses, human evaluation, rejection, revision, selection, or a subsequent question, and the AI response that followed. These cases are not a sample for estimating frequency or representativeness. In this paper, co-creative adaptation is used as a descriptive umbrella label for cases in which user adaptation, broadly construed, appears within interactions treated as Human-AI co-creation. Across the cases, with varying strength, the analysis found that (1) human evaluative agency remained present in the interaction; (2) AI responses took the form of organization or reconstruction oriented to the user's aims and interests; and (3) particularly in Cases C and D, differences in judgment or conclusion remained, dialogue continued, and those differences became material for further questions, investigation, or revision. As a secondary observation, the user also assigned value to the time spent interacting beyond the production of an artifact, after which the framing in the subsequent AI response changed. Conceptual and interactional comparison of these observations with sycophancy research suggests that user adaptation in the broad sense may not be reducible to harmful sycophancy. This study describes a limited set of naturalistic ChatGPT use cases and makes no claims about causality, internal mechanisms, frequency, or generalization to other conversational AI systems.

title: SDG12 Tweets 2024-2026
abstract: Publicly available posts mentioning #SDG12—which focuses on Sustainable Development Goal 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production)—were gathered using a custom Python script that queried the X (formerly Twitter) API. The data collection targeted the #SDG12 hashtag directly, capturing content published between January 1, 2024, and July 31, 2026. For each post, the extracted dataset recorded the raw text content, the classification of the post (original tweet, retweet, or reply), user profile details, and complete interaction counts (likes, retweets, replies, and quote tweets).

title: Adaptive Clustering Algorithm for Graph Structure Optimization – Leveraging Graph Structure Optimization for Enhanced Clustering
abstract: This paper investigates the application of adaptive clustering algorithms to improve the effectiveness of various clustering techniques. Traditional clustering methods often struggle with automatic adjustment of parameters, leading to suboptimal results. This work proposes a novel adaptive clustering algorithm that leverages graph structure optimization to enhance clustering performance. The core mechanism involves incorporating graph-based structure information into the clustering process, enabling the algorithm to identify and group data points more effectively. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through simulations and qualitative analysis, highlighting its superior performance compared to existing methods across a range of datasets. The algorithm's ability to dynamically adjust its parameters based on graph structure offers a significant advantage in identifying meaningful clusters.

title: Quantum Resonance Networks for Algorithmic Complexity Analysis
abstract: Quantum Resonance Networks (QRNs) represent a novel approach to algorithmic complexity analysis, leveraging the principles of entanglement and superposition to create dynamic, interconnected networks. This research explores the potential of QRNs as a tool for quantifying complexity, moving beyond traditional approximation methods and offering a fundamentally quantum-based assessment. The core mechanism involves establishing a network where nodes are interconnected through entanglement, generating patterns that are indicative of complex algorithmic behavior. This paper details the framework for QRNs, its underlying principles, and its potential impact on the field of algorithmic complexity.

title: Title: Probabilistic Algorithm for Bayesian Network Optimization in High Dimensional Spaces
abstract: Bayesian network optimization (BNO) is a powerful technique for discovering optimal solutions in complex systems, particularly within high-dimensional spaces. However, traditional BNO methods often struggle with the exponential growth of the search space, hindering their applicability. This paper introduces a novel probabilistic algorithm, termed Bayesian Network Optimization with Adaptive Complexity (BNOA-AC), designed to address this challenge. BNO-AC leverages a dynamically adjustable Bayesian network structure, employing probabilistic sampling to guide exploration and mitigate the computational burden associated with high-dimensional problems. The algorithm's core mechanism centers around intelligently managing the complexity of the search space, providing a computationally efficient and effective approach to optimization. This work presents a rigorous analysis of the algorithm's performance, demonstrating its efficacy through a series of simulations and comparisons to established BNO methods. The proposed approach offers a significant improvement in efficiency and robustness, promising to unlock new possibilities for optimization across various domains.

title: Core Claim: Develop a novel adaptive particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm to optimize complex physical systems, incorporating a mechanism for parameter adjustment based on environmental change, achieving a self-adaptive optimization process.
abstract: This paper introduces a new adaptive particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm designed to efficiently optimize complex physical systems. The core of this algorithm lies in its ability to dynamically adjust the PSO parameters based on observed environmental changes, creating a self-adaptive optimization process. Traditional PSO algorithms often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their effectiveness in dynamic environments. The proposed algorithm incorporates a mechanism to dynamically adjust the parameters based on observed changes, resulting in improved performance and adaptability. The paper details the algorithm's implementation, demonstrates its effectiveness through a series of simulations, and discusses its potential applications in various fields. The primary goal is to provide a robust and flexible optimization technique capable of handling complex, evolving parameter spaces.

title: Adaptive Self-Adaptive Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel learning algorithm, Adaptive Self-Adaptive Learning (ASAL), designed to optimize complex mathematical models through dynamic adjustment of learning parameters. Traditional learning algorithms often employ static parameters, limiting the potential for improved model parameter optimization. ASAL leverages the core principles of adaptive learning to dynamically adjust parameters based on the system's state, achieving a more effective model parameter refinement. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, proposes a novel mechanism for parameter adjustment, and provides a comprehensive analysis of its performance. This work represents a significant advancement in the field of model parameter optimization, particularly for intricate mathematical scenarios.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Optimization via Adaptive Constraint Distribution
abstract: Quantum-enhanced optimization leverages the unique properties of quantum mechanics to accelerate the solution of complex optimization problems. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, Quantum-Enhanced Optimization via Adaptive Constraint Distribution, designed to intelligently distribute constraint constraints during optimization. The core mechanism centers around dynamically adjusting constraint distribution based on the optimization state, aiming to improve convergence speed and overall efficiency. We explore the potential benefits of this approach, particularly in tackling problems exhibiting inherent complexity and requiring nuanced constraint management. The paper details the algorithm's design, its implementation using a quantum simulator, and preliminary results demonstrating improved convergence compared to conventional optimization methods. Keywords: Quantum Optimization, Constraint Distribution, Adaptive Algorithm, Quantum Simulation, Convergence, Optimization.

title: Based on Multi-Variable Gaussian Processes for Program Optimization (MVGPPO)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to program optimization, termed Multi-Variable Gaussian Process Optimization (MVGPPO), leveraging the power of Gaussian Processes (GPs) for global search. Traditional program optimization techniques frequently rely on local search algorithms, which can easily become trapped in local optima. MVGPPO addresses this limitation by employing GPs to model the program execution state. This allows for a probabilistic representation and facilitates a global search strategy, mitigating the risk of premature convergence. The core claim of this work is that by utilizing GPs to model program states, a comprehensive and effective global optimization strategy can be achieved. We detail the core mechanism of utilizing Gaussian Process regression to model the program's state, coupled with the probabilistic distribution afforded by GPs for the global search process. This approach demonstrates a significant improvement over conventional local search methods, particularly in complex and high-dimensional program optimization problems. The key innovation lies in the ability of the GP to represent the underlying function without requiring explicit gradient information, enabling a robust and adaptable optimization strategy. ---

title: Cognitive Computing Architecture Based on Bayesian Networks and Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel cognitive computing architecture designed to address the limitations of current systems in integrating diverse knowledge and reasoning under uncertainty. The architecture leverages the strengths of Bayesian Networks for representing prior knowledge and Reinforcement Learning for adaptive learning and experience-based reasoning. The core of the system is a dynamically updating Bayesian Network informed by reinforcement learning feedback. This approach allows the system to not only incorporate new information but also to learn optimal strategies for reasoning and decision-making. The architecture is presented with detailed mathematical formulations outlining the key components and their interactions. Specifically, we define the state space, action space, reward function, and Bayesian Network structure. The system's performance is theoretically analyzed, focusing on convergence properties and the impact of network structure on learning efficiency. The goal is to demonstrate a robust and flexible cognitive computing system capable of handling complex, uncertain environments.

title: Generative Adversarial Networks for Discovering Novel Sensor Topologies
abstract: The design of optimal sensor topologies—the arrangement and connectivity of sensors within a system—is a critical, yet often laborious, process in various fields, including robotics, environmental monitoring, and medical diagnostics. This paper proposes a novel approach utilizing Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to automate this design process. The core idea is to train a GAN where one network (the generator) proposes sensor topologies, and the other network (the discriminator) evaluates these topologies based on a defined performance metric, typically maximizing signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) or minimizing error. The system iteratively learns to generate topologies that consistently outperform existing designs, effectively discovering novel configurations. We demonstrate the feasibility and potential of this approach through theoretical analysis and a conceptual framework, outlining the key components and training strategies. The resulting framework offers a powerful tool for rapidly exploring and optimizing sensor topologies, potentially leading to significant advancements in applications requiring precise sensor arrangements.

title: 基于量子自旋的分布式量子计算算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel distributed quantum computing algorithm based on the inherent adaptability of quantum spin systems. We propose a 'Quantum Spin Distributed' algorithm that leverages quantum spin's adaptive properties to enable self-learning and optimization of quantum computers. This approach offers a paradigm shift in computational efficiency, addressing limitations of existing algorithms through a dynamically adjusted quantum state. The core mechanism centers around constructing a 'Quantum Spin Distributed' system, which uses the self-adaptive nature of quantum spin to improve the performance of quantum computations. We detail the algorithm's design, its advantages, and potential applications in diverse quantum computing tasks.

title: 基于量子自旋的神经网络的自适应学习
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of utilizing quantum spin systems to enhance the self-adaptive learning capabilities of neural networks. Traditional neural network architectures often rely on manually engineered parameters, limiting their flexibility and hindering their ability to generalize effectively across diverse datasets. We propose a novel approach that introduces quantum spin systems as a fundamental building block within the network architecture. The core mechanism involves utilizing the inherent self-adaptability of quantum spin states to dynamically adjust the network's parameters during training, leading to improved model robustness and generalization performance. This work explores the implementation of a quantum-inspired network architecture and examines its impact on key performance metrics, including accuracy and stability. The research underscores the potential of leveraging quantum mechanics to overcome limitations inherent in classical neural network training.

title: Adaptive Meta-Learning Algorithm Evolving Strategy
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to meta-learning by leveraging evolutionary algorithms. The core concept involves treating a meta-learning algorithm as an individual within an evolving population. Through iterative processes of selection, crossover, and mutation, the parameters of the meta-learning algorithm are continuously refined, ultimately leading to enhanced adaptive learning capabilities. The proposed strategy aims to overcome the limitations of traditional meta-learning methods by dynamically adjusting the learning process based on the encountered environment. This work demonstrates the potential for significantly improved performance across a range of meta-learning tasks through this evolutionary optimization process. The primary goal is to establish a robust and adaptable meta-learner that can autonomously adjust its learning strategy. The theoretical framework and the underlying mechanisms are thoroughly explained, showcasing a new paradigm in meta-learning design.

title: Neural Evolution Algorithm
abstract: This paper proposes a novel evolutionary algorithm, the Neural Evolution Algorithm (NEA), which leverages the dynamic properties of neural networks to achieve adaptive learning and optimization. The core idea is to represent individuals within the evolutionary algorithm as artificial neural networks, where the connections and plasticity of synapses are dynamically adjusted. Fitness evaluation is performed by assessing the network's performance through its connection weights and synaptic plasticity. The algorithm employs a simulation of neural networks, mimicking synaptic connections and plasticity rules to drive the evolutionary process. NEA offers a fundamentally new evolutionary mechanism by integrating the inherent dynamics of neural networks into the algorithm's framework. We demonstrate the potential of NEA in tackling complex optimization problems, emphasizing its ability to adapt and evolve solutions over time. This work provides a theoretical foundation and explores the initial design principles for NEA, laying the groundwork for future research and development.

title: Staged Hybrid Quantum-Classical Programming
abstract: Hybrid quantum-classical computing systems consist of a classical control system that sends quantum circuits and receives measurement results from a quantum co-processor. Such systems allow us to model algorithms that require the classical control system to generate quantum circuits on the fly, potentially based on prior measurement results. This is challenging, as the classical control system must generate quantum circuits that manipulate live quantum states. In this setting, the classical control system is generating further quantum circuits while the quantum co-processor is internally maintaining the state of the live qubits; this is not ideal, since this not only is costly but also introduces additional sources of noise to the live qubits. Thus, we want to minimize the latency between receiving measurement results and sending the next quantum circuit to be executed by pre-computing quantum circuits. We introduce HyQ (pronounced haiku), a multi-modal language based on adjoint logic that pre-generates quantum circuits before executing a hybrid quantum-classical program. We achieve this by separating our semantics into two distinct stages: 1) compile-time generation of quantum circuits and classical runtime code and 2) execution of the classical runtime code that instruments the quantum co-processor. This separation between stages allows us to formally guarantee that all circuit-generation logic occurs before the instrumentation logic, i.e., the actual runtime, and minimizes the idling of the quantum co-processor at runtime. We give a type system, a circuit-normalization semantics for the compile-time stage, which eagerly performs all circuit-generation logic, and a runtime semantics for HyQ that corresponds to the second stage. We prove type preservation and progress for both semantics.

title: Latent Washout? Geometric convergence and wording-style recoverability under shared continuations
abstract: When two differently worded questions are followed by the same text, their hidden states may become closer. Does that also make the original wording style harder to identify? We study this question using 96 authored everyday/formal question pairs across six domains and three frozen language models: Gemma 4 E4B IT, Phi-4-mini-instruct, and Qwen3.5-4B. Each pair has the same answer instruction and exactly matched token counts under the evaluated model's tokenizer. We compare final hidden states after a short answer anchor and after a longer supplied task continuation, producing 1,152 measurements. Mean paired cosine distance decreases by 64.0%, 40.6%, and 54.4%, respectively. Yet logistic classifiers evaluated on held-out domains identify wording style after the task continuation in 135/192, 137/192, and 138/192 cases, compared with 96/192 for token-count-only controls. Classifier accuracy rises for Gemma and falls for Phi and Qwen; descriptive intervals for these changes all include zero. The results show that geometric convergence can coexist with detectable authored style differences after controlling instruction and token-count cues. Post-hoc checks also find broader geometric contraction and readily predictable wording labels. These results do not establish selective wording loss, semantic abstraction, exact prompt recovery, or unchanged information content. We document the earlier control failures that motivated the corrected experiment. Code and data: https://github.com/theomirzakhanian/latentwashoutartifacts/tree/main

title: Information-Set Conditional Integrity Auditing for Hybrid Quantum-Classical Kernel Workflows: reproducibility artifact v1.1.0
abstract: Version 1.1.1 reproducibility artifact for the article Information-Set Conditional Integrity Auditing for Hybrid Quantum-Classical Kernel Workflows (submitted to IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing). The record contains the compact review artifact (source code, tests, locked Python 3.10 environment, derived evidence for the frozen 1.0.0 gates and the preregistered 1.1.0 reinforcement gates, figures, SHA-256 manifests, the TDSC manuscript and supplement PDFs) and a source snapshot of the tagged repository. Central claim: integrity auditability is conditional on the evidence exposed at the audited workflow boundary. Evaluation-label interventions leave feature, score and prediction evidence exactly invariant; prior-preserving exchanges also leave label marginals invariant; item-aligned trusted outcomes close the blind region. Version 1.1.0 adds null calibration with disjoint clean pools, a symmetric preprocessing ablation and cross-validated tuning of both learners, preregistered before execution. Licensing: source code under Apache-2.0; derived evidence, tables, figures and documentation under CC BY 4.0; manuscript sources and PDFs are shared as author preprints and are excluded from both licenses pending the IEEE publishing agreement (see LICENSING.md inside the artifact). Version 1.1.1 is an editorial release: it changes only the wording of the funding acknowledgement to the formula prescribed by the Spanish State Research Agency; no scientific content, results, figures, data or claims changed with respect to version 1.1.0 (10.5281/zenodo.22550853). Funding: This work is part of grant PID2024-155693NB-C43, ATHENA-AEGIS (Advanced Secure Technologies for Hybrid Quantum-Classical Environments and Applications), funded by MICIU/AEI/10.13039/501100011033 and by ERDF/EU. Verification: python software/src/experiments/verify_publication_artifact.py --root . recomputes every embedded manifest, 44 outputs, the primary counts and the calibrated label-path checks.

title: The Adaptive Parametric Clustering Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive parametric clustering algorithm designed to improve clustering quality and efficiency by dynamically adjusting cluster parameters. Traditional clustering methods often rely on predefined strategies, which struggles to effectively handle complex datasets. Our proposed algorithm leverages self-adaptive parameter tuning to optimize the cluster centers, distances, and cluster shapes, ultimately leading to enhanced clustering results. The core mechanism centers around a dynamic adjustment process that responds to the data's characteristics, enabling the algorithm to discover and refine latent structures within the data. We present a comprehensive evaluation demonstrating the superiority of this approach compared to existing methods, particularly in scenarios with high dimensionality and non-convex data.

title: Quantum Information Cryptography: A Novel Approach to Non-Linear Key Distribution
abstract: Quantum information cryptography offers the promise of unprecedented security by leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics. A critical challenge in this field is the vulnerability of existing key distribution schemes to attacks. This paper investigates a novel cryptographic model based on non-linear key distribution, aiming to address this vulnerability and enhance security. We propose a new algorithm that exploits the inherent non-linear properties of quantum systems to generate and distribute keys with enhanced resilience against various attacks. This research focuses on the design of a secure key distribution protocol, emphasizing the use of a non-linear operation to generate a key that is difficult to reverse. The core of this work lies in the implementation of a robust key allocation process that significantly improves key security through the exploitation of non-linear quantum phenomena. We present a detailed analysis of the proposed algorithm, demonstrating its potential to surpass traditional cryptographic methods in terms of security and resilience. This research explores the theoretical underpinnings of non-linear key distribution, proposes a practical implementation, and evaluates its performance through simulations and potential future investigations.

title: Title: Dimensionality Reduction via Wavefunction Sampling with Constraints
abstract: Dimensionality reduction is a fundamental challenge in many data science applications, requiring efficient methods to represent high-dimensional data while preserving essential information. Traditional dimensionality reduction techniques often suffer from limitations in preserving data integrity and can result in loss of interpretability. This paper proposes a novel approach to dimensionality reduction using wavefunction sampling, coupled with a sophisticated constraint satisfaction mechanism. We explore the potential of this method to uncover hidden structure within the data space, offering a pathway towards more meaningful and robust representations. The core of our system is a quantum state sampling algorithm that dynamically adjusts the probability distribution of wavefunction states based on predefined constraints, ensuring that the resulting representations accurately capture the underlying data patterns. We present a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's performance, demonstrating its effectiveness in reducing data dimensionality while maintaining a high degree of data fidelity. This work holds promise for applications in various fields, including image processing, natural language processing, and data visualization.

title: Title: Quantum State-Space Hybrid Neural Networks (QSS-NN)
abstract: Quantum State-Space Hybrid Neural Networks (QSS-NN) presents a novel approach to artificial neural network design, leveraging the unique capabilities of quantum mechanics to enhance learning capabilities. This paper explores the integration of quantum information processing directly into the core of a neural network architecture, aiming to overcome limitations inherent in classical models. We introduce a framework predicated on the concept of quantum state-space entanglement, utilizing quantum circuits to represent input data and enable the network to learn from correlated quantum states. The core mechanism focuses on utilizing quantum coherence as a key feature for improved data representation and learning. The resulting QSS-NN architecture demonstrates significant potential for improved performance in certain complex tasks, offering a fundamentally different perspective on neural network design. This work investigates the potential of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation.

title: Quantum Error Correction Topology Simulation Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum error correction algorithm designed to facilitate the accurate simulation of complex topological structures. Traditional topological simulations often struggle with numerical precision and the representation of intricate topologies, limiting their ability to reveal subtle features and potential errors. Our algorithm leverages quantum error correction (QEC) to enhance the fidelity of topological simulations by effectively mitigating the effects of noise and errors, leading to improved accuracy and the ability to better characterize topological properties. We propose a modified topological representation scheme that incorporates QEC principles to dynamically adjust the representation's complexity based on the level of error present, resulting in a more robust and accurate simulation. The core mechanism involves a novel quantum state encoding strategy combined with a dynamically adjusted error correction scheme, optimizing for both computational efficiency and topological fidelity. The proposed algorithm demonstrates improved performance in simulating a range of topological structures compared to existing methods, showcasing its potential for advancing the field of topological quantum computation.

abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a novel quantum algorithm optimization technique, termed Dynamic Adaptive Quantum Algorithm Optimizer (DQS-O). Traditional quantum algorithm optimization methods often rely on static optimization strategies, limiting their effectiveness in complex scenarios. DQS-O addresses this limitation by dynamically adapting the optimization process to the specific characteristics of the target quantum algorithm, leading to significantly improved results. This work explores the utilization of quantum phenomena – specifically, superposition and entanglement – to achieve enhanced optimization capabilities. We detail the core mechanism of DQS-O, outlining its iterative refinement and sensitivity to quantum state transformations, ultimately resulting in more efficient quantum computations. The paper also discusses the advantages and challenges associated with this approach, emphasizing its potential to revolutionize the design and execution of quantum algorithms.

title: Hierarchical Bayesian Network for Probabilistic Reasoning
abstract: This paper presents a novel Hierarchical Bayesian Network (HBN) designed for probabilistic reasoning, focusing on explicit modeling of uncertainty and information propagation across a hierarchy of reasoning steps. Traditional Bayesian networks often struggle with complex, interconnected reasoning, while HBNs offer a structured approach to handle uncertainty effectively. We propose a framework where nodes represent individual reasoning steps, and connections represent the influence of each step on others. The system allows for the propagation of information across the hierarchy, enabling reasoning at different levels of abstraction and improving the accuracy and interpretability of the reasoning process. The paper details the architecture, training methodology, and evaluation of this new HBN, demonstrating its potential for robust probabilistic inference.

title: Title: Adaptive Self-Design Algorithm
abstract: Adaptive Self-Design Algorithm is a novel algorithmic framework designed to automate the design and optimization of mathematical formulas, particularly within complex non-standard and nonlinear equation systems. This approach leverages a probabilistic search algorithm, incorporating reinforcement learning and genetic algorithms, to iteratively refine formula parameters and capture the intricate structure of the formula. The algorithm's key innovation lies in the development of a "probability search" mechanism, coupled with graph neural networks to enhance formula complexity understanding. This represents a significant advancement over existing automated formula design methods, which often rely on predefined rules and limited flexibility. The proposed algorithm demonstrates the potential to overcome human limitations in formula creation, offering a robust and adaptable solution for a diverse range of mathematical challenges.

title: Relational Reinforcement Learning with Graph Neural Networks for Robotics
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to robot control in complex, multi-agent environments by leveraging relational reinforcement learning (RRL) and graph neural networks (GNNs). The core idea is that robots benefit significantly from understanding and reasoning about the relationships between themselves and their surroundings. Traditional reinforcement learning methods often struggle in scenarios where the reward signal is not directly tied to individual actions but depends on the overall state and interactions within a system. Our proposed framework addresses this limitation by employing a GNN to explicitly model the relationships between robots and environmental elements. This graph representation allows the GNN to capture contextual information and relational dependencies, which are then used by the RRL algorithm to learn optimal policies. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical analysis and a conceptual framework, highlighting its potential to improve robot performance in scenarios demanding sophisticated relational reasoning. This work establishes a foundation for future research in combining relational reasoning with deep learning techniques for robust and adaptive robot control.

title: Probabilistic Quantum Error Correction (PQEC)
abstract: Quantum computing promises revolutionary advancements across numerous fields, but the inherent fragility of quantum states necessitates robust error correction techniques. Traditional methods, while effective, often struggle with scalability and require significant overhead. This paper explores a novel quantum error correction protocol, Probabilistic Quantum Error Correction (PQEC), predicated on dynamically fluctuating probability distributions across multiple qubits. Our core claim posits that this approach significantly enhances error correction rates compared to existing methods, offering a fundamentally new pathway towards more reliable quantum computations. The mechanism involves introducing a probabilistic error correction scheme that exploits the inherent randomness of quantum states to effectively detect and correct errors. This work details the protocol's architecture, mathematical underpinnings, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its potential for improved error correction.

title: Differential Geometry for Deep Learning Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of differential geometry to the optimization of deep learning models. Traditional deep learning optimization relies heavily on gradient descent methods, which can suffer from issues such as getting stuck in local minima and slow convergence rates. We propose a novel approach that leverages concepts from differential geometry, specifically curvature and geodesics, to guide the optimization process. The core idea is to interpret the loss landscape of a deep learning model as a Riemannian manifold and to use geometric properties of this manifold to define more effective optimization strategies. We present a theoretical framework for this approach, outlining how curvature information can be used to adapt learning rates and step sizes, and how geodesics can be utilized to find paths of steepest descent that are less likely to get trapped in suboptimal regions. Preliminary analysis suggests that integrating geometric insights could lead to faster and more robust convergence in deep learning training.

title: Symbolic AI with Dynamic Rule Generation and Refinement
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to symbolic artificial intelligence (AI) that addresses the limitations of traditional, manually-engineered rule-based systems. The core challenge in symbolic AI has historically been the extensive and often laborious process of crafting and maintaining a comprehensive rule set. Existing systems frequently exhibit brittleness and a lack of adaptability to changing environments. To mitigate these issues, we propose a system architecture leveraging reinforcement learning (RL) to dynamically generate and refine a symbolic rule base. The system operates by employing an RL agent that observes the system's performance and iteratively adjusts the rules to optimize its behavior. This dynamic approach significantly reduces the manual effort required for rule engineering while enhancing the system's robustness and adaptability. We detail the key components of this system, including the rule representation, the RL agent's reward function, and the rule modification mechanisms. The system's core claim is that a dynamically generated and refined rule base offers a more robust and adaptable solution compared to static, manually-engineered rule sets. The system's ability to learn and adapt to data-driven feedback represents a significant advancement in the field of symbolic AI. The presented method demonstrates a pathway toward creating AI systems that can autonomously evolve their knowledge representation, ultimately leading to greater flexibility and efficiency.

title: 基于量子纠缠的自适应概率网络
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic network architecture, termed the "Quantum Entangled Adaptive Probability Network" (QEPN), that leverages the principles of quantum entanglement to enhance computational efficiency and precision. Traditional probabilistic networks struggle with complex calculations due to inherent limitations in parallel processing and the influence of sequential processing. The QEPN utilizes entanglement to create correlated quantum states, enabling instantaneous information transfer and accelerated computation. We propose a mechanism for dynamically adjusting the entanglement strength based on the input data, allowing the network to adapt to varying computational demands and optimize probabilities with unprecedented accuracy. This paper presents a detailed analysis of the QEPN's architecture, demonstrating its potential for significantly improving the speed and accuracy of various probabilistic tasks, including Monte Carlo simulations and Bayesian inference. The theoretical foundations of entanglement-enhanced computation are discussed, and preliminary experimental results showcase the network's capabilities. We conclude with a discussion of future research directions and potential applications.

title: Probabilistic Resonance Networks for Discovering Hidden Correlations
abstract: This paper introduces Probabilistic Resonance Networks (PRNs), a novel method for discovering hidden correlations within datasets. Traditional correlation analysis techniques often struggle with identifying subtle, non-linear relationships, especially when data is noisy. PRNs address this limitation by explicitly modeling probabilistic relationships between variables and employing a "resonance" factor to amplify correlations based on shared frequency characteristics. The resonance factor, denoted as *rij*, is a function that dynamically adjusts the strength of the connection between nodes *i* and *j* based on their similarity in a frequency domain representation. The network structure is learned through a probabilistic inference process, resulting in a network where edge weights represent the strength of the probabilistic relationship, modulated by the resonance factor. The core innovation lies in combining probabilistic modeling with a resonance mechanism, allowing PRNs to uncover correlations that would be missed by conventional methods. We demonstrate the efficacy of PRNs through a theoretical framework and outline the key components of the algorithm. The algorithm's effectiveness hinges on the accurate estimation of the resonance factors and the efficient implementation of the probabilistic inference. Future research will focus on optimizing the resonance function and exploring the application of PRNs to diverse datasets.

title: TIR Biancane Paper
abstract: Mapping hydrothermal alteration mineralogy is essential for characterizing active geothermal systems and identifying prospects for geothermal energy and mineral resource assessment. The potential of thermal infrared (TIR: 8 to 13 μm) imaging spectroscopy for geothermal mineral mapping remains largely under-explored. Here we present the first ever lithological and mineralogical maps of Parco Naturalistico delle Biancane (PNB), part of the Larderello geothermal field, derived from TIR imaging spectroscopy data collected by the Hyperspectral Thermal Emission Spectrometer (HyTES). TIR data provides simultaneous information on both surface composition and temperature, enabling the combined mapping of alteration mineralogy and thermal anomalies from a single dataset. The limited rock exposure and strong lithological and alteration heterogeneity make PNB a rigorous test environment. These results establish a validated methodological and spectral reference framework for next-generation spaceborne TIR missions, advancing the use of TIR imaging spectroscopy for geothermal exploration and mineral resource assessment.

title: The Explainability–Reliability Gap in Fraud Detection: Evidence from SHAP and Permutation Importance Under Distribution Shift
abstract: This study develops an empirical audit framework for assessing the explainability–reliability gap in fraud detection: whether stable model explanations remain consistent with performance-based feature reliance under distribution shift. Using the Bank Account Fraud dataset suite, including a Base dataset and five biased variants, the study examines group-size disparity, fraud-prevalence disparity, separability bias, and temporal shift. Logistic Regression, Linear SVC, and Random Forest are benchmarked using standard classification metrics, followed by cross-variant evaluation with Logistic Regression as the interpretable baseline. SHAP is used to assess explanation stability, while permutation importance measures performance-based feature reliance. The results show that accuracy and ROC-AUC can overstate practical effectiveness under severe class imbalance; notably, Random Forest retained useful discrimination while producing near-zero recall at the evaluated threshold. SHAP feature rankings remained relatively stable across variants, particularly for address-history, identity-similarity, credit-risk, device, and behavioral variables. However, permutation importance revealed weaker and more variable reliance on several SHAP-ranked features. The limited agreement between the two measures indicates a partial explainability–reliability gap. The findings show that explanation stability alone is insufficient for evaluating trustworthy fraud detection models and should be complemented by performance-based validation under biased and shifted deployment conditions.

title: Big Data Technology in English Education and Teachers’ Professional Practices: An Explanatory Sequential Mixed-Methods Study
abstract: The increasing use of big data technologies in education has created new opportunities for English teachers to use learning information to support instructional practices. However, empirical evidence remains limited regarding how data-driven technologies are associated with teachers’ pedagogical competencies, instructional decision-making, classroom instructional performance, and reflective teaching practices. This study examines the role of big data technology in English education in relation to professional dimensions of in-service English teachers. An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was employed, and data were collected from 287 in-service English teachers in China. The quantitative data were analyzed using Descriptive Statistics and Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Qualitative data were subsequently analyzed using thematic analysis. The quantitative findings demonstrated significant positive relationships between big data technology in English education and pedagogical competencies (β = 0.622, p < 0.001), decision-making skills (β = 0.568, p < 0.001), classroom instructional performance (β = 0.546, p < 0.001), and reflective teaching practices (β = 0.551, p < 0.001). Qualitative findings showed that teachers used learning analytics to identify student needs, modify instruction, support evidence-based decisions, evaluate classroom effectiveness, and adapt subsequent teaching. However, difficulties in data interpretation, time constraints, technical infrastructure, monitoring pressure, and student-data privacy were identified as implementation challenges. The study contributes empirical evidence linking big data technology with multiple dimensions of English teachers’ professional practice. Practical recommendations include strengthening teachers’ data literacy, providing institutional technical support, allocating time for data interpretation, and establishing clear data-governance and privacy procedures.

title: Three steps into agentic AI: a preregistered feasibility study of how non-programmers cross from chatbot to agent to multi-model orchestration (Cohort 1)
abstract: Ordinary professionals now use AI by talking to a chatbot. Two further steps exist and almost nobody has taken them: running an agent that acts on your own machine, and putting one question to several models in one action instead of visiting them by hand. This study follows a cohort of non-programmers across three specific transitions and records, for each, who crosses, how long it takes, and where the rest stop. The route is unusual and is the reason the study is possible at all. Participants are not installed for. Each receives a text, pastes it into the chatbot they already use, and that chatbot walks them through installing a graphical agent on their own machine. The investigator does not touch anyone's computer. This is a feasibility study of a pathway. It measures crossing, and it records usefulness without claiming to prove it. It has no control group and makes no causal claim. It is Cohort 1 of a programme; later cohorts are registered separately.

title: Attention-Enhanced Deep Features with Heterogeneous Ensemble Learning for Glaucoma Detection
abstract: Glaucoma is a progressive optic neuropathy characterized by irreversible damage to the optic nerve, making timely diagnosis critical to prevent permanent vision loss. Although deep learning has demonstrated promising performance in automated glaucoma detection, existing approaches often overlook feature refinement, suffer from class imbalance, and rely on individual classifiers that limit prediction robustness. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a hybrid glaucoma detection framework that integrates attention-enhanced deep feature extraction with heterogeneous ensemble learning. Specifically, deep representations are extracted using InceptionV3 and subsequently refined by incorporating the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) to enhance discriminative retinal features. To improve classification robustness, the extracted features are classified using multiple machine learning models together with Single-Level Ensemble (SLE) and Double-Level Ensemble (DLE) strategies, while SMOTE combined with Tomek Links (SMOTE+TL) is employed to alleviate class imbalance. Furthermore, a systematic comparison of handcrafted, deep, and attention-enhanced deep feature representations is conducted. Experimental evaluation on two public retinal fundus datasets demonstrates that deep feature-based methods consistently outperform handcrafted feature-based methods, while the proposed attention-enhanced framework achieves the best overall performance. Furthermore, Grad-CAM visualizations confirm that the proposed model focuses on clinically relevant retinal regions, providing interpretable evidence on the model's prediction process.

title: Localize, Restart, Accelerate: Stochastic Optimization under Generalized Smoothness
abstract: We study stochastic convex optimization under asymmetric \((L_0,L_1)\)-generalized smoothness, a model motivated by machine-learning objectives whose local curvature may grow with the gradient norm. We assume an unbiased first-order oracle with additive norm-sub-Gaussian noise. Acceleration is difficult in this setting because momentum may enter regions of much larger curvature, while stochastic gradients cannot reliably certify an unrestricted trajectory. We propose \textsf{ARC-SG}, a two-phase accelerated method: Phase~I reduces excessively large gradients using a generalized-smoothness-aware stochastic step, then Phase~II solves strongly convex proximal subproblems by a restarted accelerated solver confined to certified smoothness balls. Exact proximal points do not increase the gradient norm, allowing these certificates to propagate through the outer loop. The contribution is a query-by-query certified-localization construction with explicit generalized-smoothness factors and a strongly convex restart extension. \textsf{ARC-SG} achieves, with high probability, an accelerated optimization contribution and smooth-subclass-optimal statistical dependence on accuracy, up to logarithmic and generalized-smoothness factors. Its convex accuracy exponents agree with a contemporaneous public stochastic-acceleration result under a broader smoothness and affine-variance model; our distinction is the certified geometry, explicit parameter accounting, and strongly convex guarantee. The results recover classical accelerated stochastic rates when \(L_1=0\). Experiments on objectives with unbounded gradients illustrate the two-phase mechanism and its finite-budget advantage.
