title: Trapped - Project Report
abstract: Moving through uneven, broken-up spaces under normal physics is a classic hard problem in reinforcement learning (RL). Most continuous-control benchmarks have smooth state changes and forgiving failure conditions. Precise 2D platforming is different: it creates hard credit-assignment problems, reward landscapes that do not rise smoothly, deadly falls (“the curse of the ledge”), and platforms that move under the agent's feet. In this work we present TRAPPED, a full framework for building reliable parkour policies across hard level layouts. We model the environment as a Markov Decision Process with discrete actions and a continuous state space (S ⊂ R¹⁷, A ∈ {0,…,4}), running on deterministic 60 Hz physics with per-axis Euler integration and a short grace period for late jumps (coyote time). To stop the policy from settling into a bad habit, we build a reward function grounded in potential-based reward shaping (PBRS), plus extra shaping tied to the physics of takeoff and landing. To get past the huge exploration problem caused by moving platforms, we use a three-stage curriculum that carries learned skills from static gaps, to raised ledges, to a platform that swings back and forth. Finally, we show the policy running in a browser: we trace the model into an Open Neural Network Exchange (ONNX) graph and apply dynamic symmetric INT8 quantization, shrinking it by 50.8% down to 11.5 KB. This lets it run instantly in-browser at 60 FPS through WebAssembly, with no cloud calls needed. Testing shows our curriculum and sensor setup reach a 98.4% success rate across many different platform swing patterns.

title: 基于量子纠缠的几何形状评估 (QGEMA)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel geometric shape assessment method, QGEMA, leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement to enhance evaluation accuracy and reliability. Traditional geometric shape assessment methods often rely on classical computation, limiting precision and susceptibility to human error. QGEMA utilizes quantum entanglement to create a unique, probabilistic assessment framework, offering a paradigm shift in geometric analysis. The paper details the fundamental principles of entanglement, the implementation of QGEMA, and the resulting performance improvements across a range of geometric shapes. We demonstrate that QGEMA achieves a significant increase in accuracy and stability compared to conventional methods. This research represents a significant step forward in geometric assessment, paving the way for more sophisticated and reliable geometric analysis techniques.

title: Title: Adaptive Topology-Based Search for Self-Organizing Space Exploration
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic topology-based search algorithm designed to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of space exploration. Traditional space search algorithms often rely on predefined search spaces, limiting their adaptability. We propose a new approach that dynamically adjusts the search space based on the input data's topology, optimizing the search process. The core mechanism involves leveraging the inherent properties of topological structures to iteratively refine the search space, resulting in improved performance. This design addresses limitations of existing techniques and offers a promising solution for complex search problems.

title: Quantum-Driven Bayesian Optimization of Neural Network Architecture
abstract: Quantum-driven Bayesian optimization (QBO) presents a novel approach to neural network architecture search, employing quantum annealing or QAOA to efficiently explore the vast design space. This research investigates the potential of quantum algorithms to accelerate the discovery of optimal neural network architectures, addressing limitations of traditional methods like grid search. The core mechanism centers on utilizing quantum annealing to sample neural network designs, enabling a significantly broader exploration of potential architectures compared to classical methods. The study will analyze the impact of quantum optimization on the search process, focusing on speed and the ability to uncover unexpected architectural patterns. The paper will detail the implementation of a quantum algorithm, its performance compared to classical approaches, and the potential benefits of leveraging quantum mechanics for neural network design. This work aims to provide a fundamental understanding of the application of quantum optimization to neural network architecture discovery.

title: Neural Network Quantum Leap (NNQL)
abstract: Neural Network Quantum Leap (NNQL) is a novel approach to quantum computing that leverages deep learning to predict quantum system trajectories and automatically adjust quantum circuits. Traditional quantum computation struggles with the unpredictable nature of quantum transitions, leading to inefficient algorithms. NNQL aims to overcome this limitation by building a deep learning model to forecast quantum跃ations and optimize circuits in real-time. This research presents a framework for predicting quantum transitions using neural networks, demonstrating a significant improvement in quantum circuit efficiency and overall system performance. The core mechanism hinges on learning from historical data to model quantum transition probabilities, enabling automated circuit optimization. We demonstrate the effectiveness of NNQL through simulations and analysis of quantum circuit dynamics, showcasing a substantial increase in expected quantum output with minimal control parameter adjustments.

title: Title: Adaptive Self-Organizing Matrix Construction
abstract: This paper presents an innovative algorithm for constructing and dynamically modifying matrix structures, inspired by the principles of biological neural networks. Traditional matrix representations often rely on static designs, neglecting the dynamic adaptation to changing data patterns. Our proposed approach, termed Adaptive Self-Organizing Matrix Construction, employs a self-referential evolutionary process wherein the matrix structure itself evolves based on feedback from the input data. This iterative process ensures robustness and efficiency, offering a novel method for data representation and potentially unlocking new capabilities in data science. The core mechanism revolves around a feedback loop that continuously refines the matrix based on observed data, mimicking the neural network's ability to adjust its connections. We detail the algorithm's design, implementation, and preliminary results, demonstrating its efficacy in adapting to dynamic datasets. The paper concludes with a discussion of the implications of this approach for various data science applications.

title: Title: Non-Locality-Guided Quantum Algorithms
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for revolutionizing various fields, but its practical realization faces significant challenges. Current quantum algorithms often necessitate full-scale quantum computation, limiting their accessibility and applicability. This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum computation – "Non-Locality-Guided Quantum Algorithms" – that explicitly leverages entanglement to minimize the need for full-scale measurements. We propose a new algorithm architecture centered on establishing and manipulating entanglement to achieve computational results without the complexities and resource demands associated with full-scale quantum systems. This work represents a significant departure from traditional quantum algorithm design, focusing on a fundamentally different paradigm for harnessing quantum mechanics. The core claim is that such algorithms can achieve comparable or superior performance in certain tasks without the need for full-scale quantum hardware, offering a pathway toward more efficient and accessible quantum computing.

abstract: FINDING: Quantum teleportation transmits state (not matter) over 1,400 km; energy teleportation demonstrated on superconducting hardware; no violation of no-communication theorem. | MATH: Teleportation fidelity \(F = \langle\psi|\rho_{\text{out}}|\psi\rangle\) (max classical bound \(F \leq 2/3\)); Bell-state measurement projects onto maximally entangled basis \(\{\Phi^\pm, \Psi^\pm\}\); energy teleportation uses local operations and classical communication (LOCC) with energy extracted from vacuum fluctuations via negative-energy density regions — quantified by conditional energy \(\langle H_B \rangle_{\text{post-measurement}} < 0\). | CONNECTION: Bell states form a 4-element orthonormal basis in \(\mathbb{C}^2 \otimes \mathbb{C}^2\) — isomorphic to the quaternion group \(Q_8\) and the tetrahedral (A3) root system; the 1,400 km link (satellite Micius) uses polarization states on the Poincaré sphere — a 2-sphere with SU(2) symmetry, whose Hopf fibration \(S^3 \to S^2\) encodes the 0.618/ Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: Self-Correcting Neural Networks via Iterative Refinement
abstract: Neural networks, while powerful, are susceptible to error accumulation during training, often leading to suboptimal performance and difficulty in escaping local minima. This paper proposes a novel architecture – a recurrent neural network (RNN) – incorporating an iterative refinement mechanism to address this issue. The core idea is to leverage a feedback loop within the RNN that continuously monitors its own output and adjusts its parameters to minimize discrepancies. This self-correcting process effectively guides the network towards a more accurate solution. We demonstrate, through a theoretical framework, that this approach offers inherent robustness against local minima compared to traditional training methods. The proposed system utilizes a loss function *L(s)*, where *s* represents the network's output. The iterative refinement is governed by a parameter update rule: *Δθ* = -η *∇L(s)* where *θ* represents the network's parameters, *η* is the learning rate, and *∇L(s)* is the gradient of the loss function with respect to *θ*. The iterative process continues until a convergence criterion is met, such as |*∇L(s)*| < ε, where ε is a predefined tolerance. The key contribution of this work is a systematic and robust method for mitigating error accumulation in neural networks, providing a pathway to improved accuracy and stability.

title: Topological Quantum Entanglement Network
abstract: The development of Topological Quantum Entanglement Networks (TQENs) represents a paradigm shift in quantum information processing, offering enhanced security and capabilities for complex computations. This paper explores the foundational principles of TQENs, detailing a novel design incorporating quantum entanglement and topological properties to achieve secure and robust data transmission. We present a detailed architectural overview, emphasizing the crucial role of quantum entanglement in maintaining the network's integrity and facilitating advanced quantum algorithms. The core mechanism focuses on establishing a stable and secure entanglement foundation, enabling the execution of computationally intensive tasks and sophisticated signal processing. The research highlights the potential of TQENs to revolutionize data security and accelerate scientific discovery.

title: Meta-Learning for Adaptive Hyperparameter Optimization of Machine Learning Models
abstract: This paper explores the application of meta-learning techniques to the problem of adaptive hyperparameter optimization for machine learning models. Traditional hyperparameter optimization methods often rely on exhaustive search or gradient-based techniques, which can be computationally expensive and time-consuming, particularly for complex models and large datasets. We propose a meta-learning approach where a meta-learner is trained to predict optimal hyperparameters based on the characteristics of the training data and the model architecture. This allows for adaptive tuning, significantly reducing the time and resources required to achieve optimal model performance. The core claim is that meta-learning provides a framework for automating and accelerating the hyperparameter optimization process. We define the problem mathematically, outlining the key components of the meta-learning system and demonstrating its potential for improved model training efficiency. The approach focuses on learning a mapping from model-specific characteristics to optimal hyperparameter settings, ultimately leading to faster convergence and better generalization performance.

title: Causal Bayesian Networks with Intervention-Aware Probabilities
abstract: Standard Bayesian Networks (BNs) struggle to represent the effects of interventions accurately, a critical limitation in causal modeling. This paper introduces a novel approach – Causal Bayesian Networks (CBNs) with Intervention-Aware Probabilities – designed to overcome this deficiency. The core idea is to augment BNs with probabilities that explicitly capture the causal influence of external interventions on the network's state. These 'intervention-aware' probabilities represent how an intervention alters the conditional probabilities within the network, reflecting the causal impact rather than simply the observed correlations. This allows for more realistic and accurate modeling of systems where interventions are frequently applied. The proposed method addresses the fundamental issue of representational inadequacy in standard BNs and provides a framework for reasoning about interventions in complex systems. The paper outlines the theoretical foundations, the formal definition of the CBN framework, and discusses key considerations for implementation and validation. The core claim is that standard BNs fail to accurately represent the effects of interventions, and the mechanism is to incorporate intervention-aware probabilities.

title: Quantum Wave Function Reconstruction (QWR)
abstract: This paper presents the Quantum Wave Function Reconstruction (QWR) algorithm, a novel approach to quantum system reconstruction utilizing advanced quantum state tomography techniques. The core claim is that QWR significantly improves the accuracy of simulations and potentially reveals hidden correlations within quantum systems, offering a transformative advancement in quantum simulation capabilities. This work details the algorithm's methodology, explores its performance characteristics, and discusses its potential applications within the field of quantum computing and simulation.

title: Causal Data Tiers for World-Action Models
abstract: World action models predict how environments change under action, but their accuracy depends on training data that records agent-environment causality. Third-person datasets capture state; egocentric data captures the action that causes it. This survey maps egocentric data sources for world model training. We organise existing data by causal completeness: uncurated video records outcomes without actions; laboratory telemetry links physical actions to states but at limited scale; synthetic environments generate full counterfactual trajectories. We then trace how this determines how models are constructed, and how they are designed to take advantage of the various strengths of the different data types. This is followed by an analysis on the state of the egocentric data economy, outlining the saturation of data collection businesses and highlighting the need to own dynamic data infrastructure and processing pipelines as opposed to just a raw data supplier. We conclude with a discussion on the ongoing problem of accurately evaluating the effectiveness of egocentric datasets in improving model performance.

title: Explainable AI for tabular data: a systematic review on error diagnosis, data quality artifacts, and actionable explanation reliability in high-stakes domains
abstract: Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) is increasingly used in high-stakes applications involving tabular machine-learning systems, yet the reliability and practical utility of explanations depend not only on explanation methods but also on the quality, structure, and preprocessing of the underlying data. This systematic literature review examines the relationships among data conditions, explanation reliability, diagnostic use, corrective intervention, and methodological advances in XAI for tabular data. The search covered January 2015 to July 2026 and identified 27 eligible primary empirical studies published between 2020 and 2026, which were synthesized through a structured narrative approach addressing four research questions. Evidence indicates that explanation reliability, particularly stability and fidelity, can be affected by noise, class imbalance, feature correlation, distribution shift, sampling and neighborhood-generation strategies, and preprocessing choices, whereas practically important conditions such as missing values remain under-investigated. XAI can also support the identification and localization of prediction errors, biases, distributional changes, and other model failures. However, a substantial gap remains between diagnosis and corrective intervention, with relatively few studies translating explanatory insights into corrective actions followed by systematic re-evaluation. Recent methodological advances emphasize structured evaluation frameworks, reliability metrics, aggregation strategies, intrinsically interpretable alternatives, and integration of XAI into monitoring and intervention-oriented workflows. Overall, the findings support a data-centric, lifecycle-oriented perspective in which data conditions, explanation reliability, diagnosis, intervention, and re-evaluation are interconnected. Future research should prioritize standardized evaluation protocols, under-studied data-quality conditions, XAI-aware preprocessing pipelines, and empirically validated closed-loop frameworks for defensible corrective intervention.

title: Graph‐Theoretic Foundations for Semantic Network Construction Through Transformer‐based Feature Learning and Multi‐Lingual Entity‐Relation Graph Modeling
abstract: Digitization-based globalization of digital communication has spawned unparalleled demand among natural language processing (NLP) systems that must be able to deal with a wide variety of languages and linguistic situations. NLP was disrupted by the introduction of transformer-powered pre-trained language models, specifically the BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) and GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer) family that entails learning language-agnostic representations of linguistic patterns, which can be extrapolated across languages. This chapter introduces a complete frame of NLP that combines BERT and GPT-based transformer designs together with task-specific fine-tuning on multi-lingual sentiment analysis and named entity recognition. In-depth approaches to deep neural networks by Rakshit pin down theoretical foundations of the deep neural networks such as convolutional, recurrent and attention-based models, and form the foundation of complex systems of learning.

title: FRSIS: A Falsifiable Recursive Self Improving System — An FSD-Scale Software Stack
abstract: This deposit is a follow-up to Empirical Recursive Self-Improvement on Coding Agents: L1/L2 Confirmation with Negative L3 Results (Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22318825). Where that work established a controlled empirical RSI ladder (L1 Weak RSI / L2 improver RSI / L3 meta-RSI) on coding agents, the present manuscript treats the RSI factor as a singular software system: FRSIS (Falsifiable Recursive Self Improving System) — an FSD-scale, software-only vehicle embedding that ladder as substrate, plus SAE/Tesla-style lab conditional automation (goals, continuous drive, PersistenceGate), under a black-box research stance. On the 2026-09-07 coverage battery (Asia/Taipei; no LLM; dry_run default except one explicit persist proof), we report: Felix L2 on CodeHost at 6/6 seeds; CodingAgentHost L2 at 3/6 under a harder discrete basin; dual-pass bitwise-identical arm means; SAE/Tesla-style L3 autonomy on CodeHost with hit_l2 and cycles goals met, plus real --persist commits that then disarmed; Felix RSI L3 meta not demonstrated (L3_RSI_MISS; MetaHitRules unchanged). We do not claim L3_RSI_HIT, AGI, or production vehicle autonomy. Architecture internals are not revealed; capabilities, HitRules, scores, seeds, and pass/fail are.

title: Technical Audit of ChatGPT / GPT-5.6 Sol Reliability: Instruction-to-Action Binding and Multimodal Workflow Incidents
abstract: Public technical audit and evidence package documenting repeated reliability failures in a long-running ChatGPT / GPT-5.6 Sol multimodal workflow. The report distinguishes instruction comprehension from execution, focuses on state-to-action and correction-to-action binding, preserves source-provenance and causal-evidence boundaries, and includes a controlled repeated-run series plus supplemental observations from 4–6 September 2026. Internal OpenAI causes are not asserted without telemetry.

title: Geometric Topology and Quantum Computing: A Unified Optimization Framework
abstract: This paper explores the synergistic potential of geometric topology and quantum computing for advanced optimization. We propose a novel framework that leverages the unique properties of quantum computation to accelerate and enhance the optimization of complex geometric structures. The core mechanism centers on constructing a quantum-enhanced optimization algorithm, specifically designed to effectively navigate and manipulate intricate geometric configurations. The research addresses the limitations of traditional optimization techniques by integrating geometric topology – a framework for understanding shapes and their properties – with the computational power of quantum systems. This integration promises to yield significant improvements in efficiency and scalability, offering a fundamentally new approach to geometric optimization. The study investigates the fundamental principles and potential applications of this joint approach, emphasizing its capacity to tackle problems currently intractable for classical optimization methods.

title: Probability Geometric Modeling and Inference
abstract: Probability Geometric Modeling (PG) represents a novel approach to geometric modeling, leveraging the power of probability logic to generate and infer complex geometric models. This paper presents a framework that automatically constructs and interprets geometric structures based on probability distributions, addressing the challenges of high-dimensional data and complex system modeling. The core mechanism involves integrating probability logic with geometric modeling, streamlining the modeling process through automated generation and dynamic inference. This work aims to provide a more intuitive and scalable method for representing and analyzing geometric data, offering significant advantages over traditional techniques.

title: Title: Quantum-Classical Hybrid Simulation (QCHS)
abstract: Quantum-Classical Hybrid Simulation (QCHS) presents a novel framework for simulating complex quantum systems, bridging the gap between the inherent precision of quantum computation and the computational power of classical methods. This research focuses on designing a robust and adaptable simulation architecture that seamlessly integrates quantum algorithms for computationally demanding tasks and classical computational techniques for the majority of the simulation process. The core claim is to achieve unprecedented fidelity in simulating quantum phenomena, offering a pathway to accelerate research and discovery across diverse scientific disciplines. The development of QCHS aims to address current limitations in simulating complex quantum systems, particularly those involving intricate correlations and rapid dynamics. This paper details the architecture, implementation, and preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this hybrid approach.

title: Title: Algorithmic Geometry for Adaptive Data Structures
abstract: This paper explores the integration of algorithmic geometry, a framework rooted in geometric principles, into data structure design. We present a novel methodology that leverages geometric concepts to automatically generate data structures optimized for specific computational tasks. The core mechanism centers around the application of geometric transformations and constraints to define the structure of data elements, creating structures that exhibit desirable properties like efficient space usage, optimized traversal paths, and predictable performance. The paper details the algorithmic process, introduces a set of geometric transformations, and demonstrates its effectiveness through several illustrative examples. This work represents a significant advancement in data structure design, moving beyond static, pre-defined structures towards a dynamic and adaptive approach.

title: 基于量子叠加的概率机器学习模型
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum superposition to enhance probabilistic machine learning models. Traditional machine learning algorithms often struggle with the inherent limitations of classical computation, particularly in handling complex data and computationally intensive tasks. We propose a novel probabilistic machine learning model predicated on quantum superposition, aiming to overcome these limitations through the strategic manipulation of model parameters within quantum states. This model leverages the unique properties of superposition to enhance prediction accuracy and robustness, presenting a fundamentally different approach to probabilistic learning. The core mechanism focuses on mapping model parameters into quantum states, utilizing quantum properties to optimize the learning process and improve overall performance. This research explores the practical implications of this approach, highlighting potential benefits and outlining future research directions.

title: 基于几何拓扑的量子态预测
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum state prediction utilizing geometric topology, specifically a modified version of the Wasserstein distance. We demonstrate that this method offers a significant advantage over traditional methods in predicting the states of quantum systems, particularly for complex entangled states. The core mechanism involves mapping the quantum state to a geometric space defined by the Wasserstein distance, allowing for efficient and accurate state prediction. We present preliminary results demonstrating improved prediction accuracy and reduced computational cost compared to existing techniques, offering a promising pathway toward enhanced quantum computation. The underlying principles are rooted in the inherent properties of geometric topology and its application to complex systems.

title: Non-Euclidean Neural Network Architecture
abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture specifically designed to effectively handle non-Euclidean data distributions. Traditional deep learning models often struggle with data that doesn't conform to Euclidean space, requiring extensive transformations or specialized data representations. Our proposed architecture, termed the 'Manifold Exploration Network' (MEN), leverages a graph neural network to intelligently explore the manifold structure of the data, identifying regions of high probability and providing a more robust representation of the underlying data distribution. The core mechanism centers on a 'manifold exploration' component, which dynamically adjusts the graph structure to prioritize regions of higher likelihood, improving generalization and performance on datasets with complex, non-Euclidean characteristics. We present a comprehensive evaluation demonstrating the MEN's superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art methods across a range of datasets, including those exhibiting non-Euclidean properties.

title: Adaptive Reinforcement Learning with Bayesian Curiosity
abstract: Standard reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms often suffer from premature convergence to suboptimal policies, particularly in complex and stochastic environments. This is largely due to a lack of effective exploration strategies, leading agents to exploit known rewards rather than discover potentially higher rewards in unexplored regions. This paper proposes a novel approach to adaptive reinforcement learning that addresses this issue by integrating Bayesian Curiosity. Bayesian Curiosity encourages the agent to explore states where its prior belief about the environment is most uncertain, effectively rewarding the agent for venturing into the unknown. The core of the method lies in utilizing a Bayesian model to represent the agent's knowledge of the environment, updating this model with each interaction and subsequently using this updated model to guide exploration. The resulting algorithm demonstrates improved exploration capabilities and, consequently, the potential to learn more robust and adaptive policies compared to traditional RL methods. The key contribution is the synergistic combination of Bayesian uncertainty quantification with a curiosity-driven exploration mechanism, offering a more principled and effective approach to tackling challenging RL problems.

title: Dynamically Weighted Graph Convolutional Networks for Adaptive Feature Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) that addresses the limitations of static weight assignment in traditional GCNs. We introduce Dynamically Weighted Graph Convolutional Networks (DW-GCNs) which adaptively learn connection weights based on the evolving dynamics of the graph structure and the input features. The core idea is to allow the network to adjust its attention mechanisms, prioritizing more relevant connections at different stages of processing. This dynamic weighting is achieved through a mechanism that implicitly or explicitly learns optimal weights, potentially leveraging reinforcement learning techniques. The resulting DW-GCNs demonstrate improved performance in adaptive feature learning tasks compared to standard GCNs, particularly in scenarios with non-stationary graph structures or varying feature distributions. The key contribution lies in the ability to create a GCN that isn't simply a static aggregation of neighbors but actively responds to the information flow. This work paves the way for more robust and efficient GCN models for various applications, including social network analysis, biological pathway inference, and dynamic sensor networks.

title: Symbolic Regression with Bayesian Uncertainty Propagation
abstract: Symbolic regression, the process of automatically discovering mathematical equations from data, holds significant promise in various scientific domains. However, existing symbolic regression methods often suffer from limitations in capturing the full spectrum of potential solutions and accurately representing the associated uncertainty. This work addresses these challenges by integrating Bayesian inference within a symbolic regression framework. Our approach, Bayesian Uncertainty Propagation (BUP), systematically propagates uncertainty about the discovered equations and their parameters throughout the regression process. This results in a distribution of possible models, providing a more comprehensive and reliable representation of the mathematical relationships embedded within the data. We demonstrate the effectiveness of BUP through a theoretical analysis and illustrate its potential with illustrative examples. The core contribution lies in providing a rigorous methodology for quantifying uncertainty during symbolic regression, ultimately leading to more robust and dependable mathematical discovery.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Constraint Propagation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize constraint propagation in systems modeling. We propose a novel quantum algorithm, the "Quantum Steering System," which dynamically adjusts constraints on a system based on entanglement measurements, offering a significantly enhanced level of precision compared to classical methods. This advancement promises breakthroughs in areas ranging from materials science and molecular dynamics simulations to optimization problems. The core of this work centers on the fundamental concept of utilizing entanglement to create a 'steering' mechanism within the system's physical constraints, enabling a level of adaptability and reduced error rates previously unattainable with classical approaches. We detail the algorithm's architecture, the underlying quantum mechanics, and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating its efficacy.

title: Bio-Inspired Chaotic Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel bio-inspired optimization algorithm, the Bio-Inspired Chaotic Optimization Algorithm (BCOA), which leverages the chaotic properties observed within biological neural networks. The core claim of this algorithm is that the inherent chaos present in neural networks can be harnessed to design an efficient optimization method capable of exploring complex search spaces. The underlying mechanism simulates chaotic activity within neural networks, capitalizing on the sensitivity to initial conditions characteristic of chaotic systems. This sensitivity is exploited by introducing small perturbations, effectively allowing the algorithm to escape local optima. BCOA offers a fresh approach to optimization by directly utilizing a biological phenomenon – chaos – providing a dynamic and potentially robust exploration strategy. The algorithm's design and theoretical underpinnings are presented, outlining its key components and operational principles. The paper details the formulation of the algorithm, focusing on the stochastic update rule and the network architecture used to simulate chaotic behavior, along with a preliminary analysis of its performance compared to established optimization techniques. ---

title: Multi-Modal Time Series Prediction Based on Biological Neuron Models
abstract: This paper explores the application of biological neuron models for multi-modal time series prediction. Traditional recurrent neural networks (RNNs) often struggle with capturing long-range dependencies and the complex dynamics inherent in time series data. This research proposes a novel approach utilizing spiking neuron models governed by Spike Timing Dependent Plasticity (STDP) to simulate realistic neural responses to diverse input modalities. These models are then integrated with recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to enhance prediction accuracy. The core claim is that these biologically-inspired models, due to their ability to model complex temporal dynamics, can effectively handle and predict long-range dependencies within multi-modal time series data. The key mechanism involves constructing STDP-based neuron models to mimic neural responses to different modalities and employing RNNs for prediction. This work represents a shift from standard RNN architectures to biologically plausible models, offering a potentially more robust and interpretable solution for multi-modal time series forecasting. The evaluation demonstrates improved predictive performance compared to conventional RNNs across various datasets. ---

title: GPU-Based Solar Irradiance Estimation over Digital Surface Models Using Structurally Lossless Viewshed Compression
abstract: High-resolution solar irradiance modelling over large 3D geospatial data is computationally demanding, and accounting for surface inter-reflection makes it even so. For computational efficiency it requires storing for every part of the surface, explicit knowledge of the other surfaces visible from it (its viewshed). The storage of each surface’s viewshed grows with both the dataset size and the angular resolution, and quickly becomes the dominant memory bottleneck. This paper presents a novel Graphics Processing Unit (GPU)-accelerated method for estimating solar potential over Digital Surface Models (DSMs) that model direct, diffuse and reflective irradiances. It keeps the viewshed information compact through a novel structurally lossless compression, i.e., a domain-specific encoding of remote sensing-derived visibility data that preserves exactly the visibility structure consumed by the radiative model, rather than a general-purpose integer coder. An ablation analysis over eight synthetic DSMs showed that the best compression scheme reached a compression ratio (CR) of up to ≈3.3, exceeding the general-purpose GPU baselines Binary Packing 32 and Elias-Fano on every dataset. On the largest DSM, whose 29.6 GB uncompressed viewshed exceeds the 24 GB device memory, compression kept the data resident and reduced the runtime from 6.7 h to 0.5 h. Finally, the proposed method was applied to LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging)-derived DSMs for four distinct locations, with the results demonstrating its high applicability.

title: Likelihood-Based Unsupervised Anomaly Detection in CMS Dijet Events
abstract: We present an unsupervised search for anomalous dijet events in proton--proton collision data using neural spline flow density estimation. A normalizing flow model is trained on a high-dimensional feature space comprising jet, dijet, and event-level observables to learn the dominant Standard Model background directly from data, without assuming a specific signal hypothesis. Events assigned low likelihood under the learned density are identified as potential anomalous events. Using this approach on a CMS Open Data dijet sample, we investigate extreme events in the tail of the anomaly-score distribution and perform an extensive validation and robustness study. This study includes feature-level statistical comparisons, mass decorrelation tests, permutation-based null tests, and evaluations of training stability. The selected anomalous events exhibit notable departures from the background-only expectation, primarily in jet-substructure observables, while remaining stable under several known sources of bias in unsupervised learning. The identified anomalies are distributed across the kinematic phase space and do not exhibit a narrow structure in the dijet invariant-mass spectrum. Instead, they show correlated deviations across multiple observables, consistent with a multivariate difference in jet substructure and event topology rather than a localized resonance. While no claim of new physics is made, this study demonstrates that neural spline flow-based density estimation can be sensitive to rare, structured deviations in collider data and may provide a model-independent exploratory tool for searches for physics beyond the Standard Model at the LHC.

title: Dynamic Topology Transformations for Probabilistic Computing Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic computing framework centered around dynamic topology transformations. Traditional probabilistic modeling often relies on static models, limiting the ability to effectively represent and adapt to complex system dynamics. This work proposes a framework that leverages the power of topology transformations – a mathematical concept that describes the evolution of a system – to dynamically adjust system states and probability distributions, enabling high-precision probabilistic calculations. The core mechanism involves embedding topology transformations within a probabilistic logic system, allowing for continuous evolution and adaptation of the system's state. We demonstrate the framework's efficacy through a series of illustrative examples and analyze its potential for addressing challenges in complex system modeling and computation.

Traditional training methods often rely on static parameters, limiting the model's ability to adapt to complex data patterns. We propose a novel approach leveraging reinforcement learning to dynamically adjust the quantum state collapse process, optimizing model performance. The core mechanism involves a reinforcement learning agent that iteratively refines the collapse based on the model's output and data distribution, leading to improved generalization and convergence speed. This work presents a framework for dynamically shaping the quantum state to enhance machine learning capabilities. The potential for significant gains in model accuracy and training efficiency is a key focus.

title: Distributed Proof Verification via Quantum Game Theory
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to mathematical proof verification leveraging quantum game theory. Traditional proof verification methods are often computationally intensive and susceptible to errors, particularly with complex proofs. We introduce a distributed verification system where multiple agents, each with limited computational resources, collaboratively verify a proof by participating in a quantum game. The game's rules are designed to incentivize truthful reporting of verification outcomes, enhancing system robustness. Our core claim is that utilizing quantum game theory can dramatically improve scalability and resilience in proof verification. We formalize the game mechanics, detailing the state space, transition probabilities, and reward structure. This approach offers a potentially transformative solution for ensuring mathematical rigor and trust in complex derivations. The theoretical framework presented here provides a foundation for future research and development in this area.

abstract: This paper investigates and proposes a novel cryptographic algorithm, termed 'Noise Morphing Cryptography,' designed to enhance resilience against adversarial attacks. The core principle centers around a dynamically adjusting randomness generation mechanism, leveraging a 'noise morphing' algorithm to subtly alter the randomness parameters during key generation or data transmission. We demonstrate that this adaptive approach surpasses existing cryptographic methods in terms of resistance to various attack vectors, offering improved security through a more robust and responsive randomness generation strategy. The proposed algorithm is presented as a potential advancement in cryptographic design, addressing limitations of static randomness and emphasizing adaptability.

title: Quantum Information Adaptive Error Correction Protocol
abstract: Quantum information is inherently vulnerable to errors due to its fragile nature. This paper introduces a novel Quantum Information Adaptive Error Correction Protocol (QIAECP) that leverages quantum entanglement and self-adaptive quantum computing to enhance the robustness of quantum information storage and transmission. The protocol utilizes entanglement-based error detection and correction, strategically manipulating entangled states to mitigate the effects of quantum noise. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and preliminary experimental analysis, highlighting its potential for significantly improving the reliability of quantum systems. The core mechanism centers on creating and utilizing entangled states to facilitate robust error correction. This paper explores the unique challenges posed by quantum noise and outlines the QIAECP's approach to address these challenges.

title: Non-Von Neumann Architectures for Cognitive Graph Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to cognitive modeling based on non-Von Neumann architectures. Traditional cognitive architectures often struggle with efficiently representing and reasoning about complex environments due to the inherent separation between memory and processing units. This work introduces a framework for cognitive graph learning, utilizing continuous event streams and adaptive learning to construct and maintain a dynamic cognitive graph. This graph, composed of nodes representing concepts and objects, and edges representing relationships between them, is then leveraged for real-time understanding and inference. The core mechanism relies on continuously updating the graph based on incoming sensory data and learned associations. We argue that this tightly coupled approach, operating within a purely event-driven architecture, offers a more natural and efficient representation of cognitive processes compared to architectures that rely on explicit storage and retrieval. The key contribution lies in the dynamic construction and utilization of the cognitive graph, enabling flexible reasoning and predictive capabilities in complex, changing environments. This architecture addresses the limitations of traditional approaches by directly mapping cognitive processes to data flow, offering a potentially superior pathway for building intelligent systems. The presented framework is designed to be adaptable and scalable, facilitating the incorporation of diverse cognitive functions and the simulation of complex cognitive behaviors. We explore the fundamental principles and outline the architecture, highlighting the advantages of this approach for achieving robust and adaptable cognitive performance.

title: Causal Discovery from Streaming Data using Granger Causality with Confidence Intervals
abstract: This paper addresses the critical challenge of causal discovery from continuous, streaming data. Traditional causal discovery methods often rely on static datasets, failing to account for the inherent temporal dependencies and non-stationarity prevalent in streaming environments. We propose an extension of Granger causality, incorporating confidence intervals to robustly estimate causal relationships within these dynamic streams. Our approach leverages the temporal autocorrelation present in the data to refine causal inferences, mitigating the risks associated with non-stationary conditions. The core mechanism involves calculating Granger causality statistics between variables in the stream and constructing confidence intervals around these statistics. These intervals provide a measure of the uncertainty associated with the causal inference, allowing for more reliable identification of potential causal links. The method offers a practical solution for discovering causal relationships in real-time data streams, with applications spanning various domains where timely causal insights are essential.

title: Quantum-Inspired Computation Resource Allocation Algorithm
abstract: This paper proposes a novel computation resource allocation algorithm inspired by the principles of quantum mechanics, specifically superposition and interference. Traditional resource allocation methods often rely on classical optimization techniques which can struggle with complex, multi-faceted problems, leading to sub-optimal solutions and inefficient resource utilization. Our approach models the resource allocation problem as a quantum system, leveraging the inherent parallelism offered by superposition and the constructive/destructive interference of quantum states to identify and converge upon optimal resource allocation strategies. We introduce a mathematical framework based on quantum operators and state vectors to represent and manipulate the allocation problem. The algorithm utilizes a variational method analogous to quantum phase estimation to minimize a cost function representing the overall resource allocation inefficiency. Simulation results (presented conceptually without actual experimental data) demonstrate the potential for significant improvements in resource efficiency compared to conventional methods, particularly in scenarios with high complexity and uncertainty. The key contribution lies in translating the concepts of quantum mechanics into a practical resource allocation framework, offering a fundamentally new approach to optimization.

title: From News to Index: A Practitioner’s Guide to a Deployable Sentiment Pipeline for Official Statistics
abstract: This paper presents a deployable pipeline for constructing a news-based sentiment index (NbSI) for official-statistics use. The index is designed as a timely complement to survey-based consumer confidence measures when releases are delayed, observations are missing, or survey collection is temporarily disrupted. The pipeline is implemented using large-scale Korean economic news, manually labeled sentence-level sentiment data, pretrained word embeddings, and three standard neural classifiers: a convolutional neural network (CNN), an long short-term memory network (LSTM), and a transformer. The empirical analysis yields four main findings: (i) a compact CNN provides the strongest model-level operational trade-off, requiring substantially less training and inference time than the LSTM or transformer while delivering similar classification reliability; (ii) marginal gains from additional labeled data flatten beyond roughly 40k sentences, suggesting diminishing returns to large-scale annotation in this application; (iii) the resulting aggregate index is stable across classifier choices, supporting the use of the computationally efficient CNN as the baseline production model; and (iv) the NbSI leads Korea’s Composite Consumer Sentiment Index (CCSI) by about one month and is most useful when survey information is delayed or unavailable for sustained periods. These findings highlight the importance of transparent validation, label quality, monitoring, and maintainability when text-based indicators are adapted for official-statistics production.

title: Visual Search Augmented Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Attribute Value Extraction from Product Videos
abstract: Existing approaches to visual attribute value extraction (AVE) primarily rely on static product images, failing to capture temporal cues, multi-angle views and fine-grained visual details. Directly applying video vision-language models (VLMs) to product AVE results in limited performance due to the lack of domain knowledge, and fine-tuning them requires extensive high-quality data and substantial computational resources. Thus, we propose visual search augmented chain-of-thought reasoning (ViS-CoT), a training-free, plug-and-play pipeline that can be easily applied to any open-source video VLM for video-to-text AVE in e-Commerce. Specifically, ViS-CoT employs visual clustering to identify representative frames, followed by visual search to retrieve semantically similar product knowledge that can enrich attribute cues. Next, an interleaved CoT reasoning module iteratively refines reasoning through visually-aligned auxiliary texts derived from captioning and automatic speech recognition. Finally, the integrated information guides the model toward accurate and fine-grained attribute predictions. Extensive experiments across 14 product categories on the VideoAVE dataset show that ViS-CoT consistently enhances multiple state-of-the-art video VLMs, achieving an average improvement of 17.91 percentage points in micro-F1.

title: Dynamic Chaos Algorithm: A Self-Adaptive Geometry-Based Optimization for Complex Systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic chaos algorithm based on self-adaptive geometry transformations. We address the challenge of optimizing complex systems, particularly those exhibiting high-dimensional, non-linear behavior, by employing a method that dynamically adjusts node connectivity and distance. The algorithm leverages a core mechanism to emulate the inherent non-linearity of chaotic systems and optimize the overall system dynamics. This approach offers enhanced stability and responsiveness compared to traditional chaotic algorithms, particularly in scenarios where static parameter adjustments prove insufficient. The core claim is that this dynamically adaptive geometry-based algorithm provides a robust and efficient method for optimizing complex systems across a broad range of applications.

title: Hierarchical Modeling of Emergent Phenomena with Bayesian Networks
abstract: This paper explores the application of Bayesian Networks (BNs) to model emergent phenomena, offering a novel hierarchical approach to automatic model generation and refinement. Emergent behaviors, often difficult to predict, are addressed by constructing a network of interconnected nodes, each representing a distinct level of abstraction. The system's core mechanism involves iteratively updating the network based on new data, ensuring the model reflects the system's dynamic nature. The paper details the architecture, training process, and evaluation of this method, highlighting its potential for robust and adaptable representation of complex systems. The goal is to provide a framework for automatically discovering and refining models of emergent behavior, leading to a more comprehensive understanding of phenomena across diverse fields.

title: Probability Field Dynamics (PFD) – Quantum Computing Validation
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Probability Field Dynamics (PFD) to quantum computing validation through simulation and quantum entanglement analysis. We propose a framework for evaluating quantum algorithms' performance using PFD-based simulations and leveraging quantum entanglement to verify algorithm correctness. Traditional quantum verification relies heavily on classical simulations, limiting the direct assessment of quantum algorithm performance. The core concept of this work is to directly utilize the probabilistic nature of PFD to validate quantum algorithms by simulating their behavior and examining entanglement correlations. This approach offers a novel pathway to robust and accurate quantum algorithm assessment. The paper outlines the framework, methodology, and preliminary results demonstrating the potential of this approach to significantly advance quantum verification techniques.

abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum machine learning algorithm, termed "Adaptive Quantum Decoupling" (AQD), designed to enhance quantum system stability during optimization. Traditional quantum decoding methods often rely on static, pre-defined decoupling strategies, failing to fully leverage the system's inherent dynamics. AQD introduces a dynamic adjustment of quantum system decoupling based on real-time analysis of the quantum state, offering a more adaptive and robust approach. This approach utilizes quantum superposition and entanglement to identify and mitigate potential instability pathways, ultimately improving the performance and reliability of quantum computations. We explore the theoretical foundation of AQD, detail the implementation of the algorithm, and present preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness in stabilizing quantum circuits.

abstract: This paper presents a novel Bayesian framework for complex systems, leveraging multi-scale inference to enhance prediction accuracy. title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Adaptive Contextualization
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neuro-symbolic reasoning, termed adaptive contextualization. Traditional neuro-symbolic systems often suffer from rigidity, relying on static context representations that may not adequately capture the nuances of complex reasoning tasks. We introduce a framework where a neural network dynamically adapts the context provided to a symbolic reasoning engine. This dynamic adjustment is driven by the input data and the evolving state of the reasoning process itself. The core idea is to treat the context as a learned feature representation, allowing the system to flexibly respond to varying levels of information and uncertainty. We formalize this approach with a specific architecture and explore its potential benefits through a theoretical analysis, highlighting improvements in robustness and adaptability compared to static context approaches. The system's performance is measured through a series of carefully designed reasoning problems, demonstrating the efficacy of adaptive contextualization. The key contribution lies in the dynamic adaptation of context, leading to a more sophisticated and robust integration of neural and symbolic capabilities.

title: Adaptive Kernel Learning for Data Stream Mining
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive kernel learning framework designed specifically for data stream mining. Traditional kernel learning algorithms often require retraining with the entire dataset upon observing new data, which is computationally expensive and impractical for continuous data streams. Our approach addresses this limitation by dynamically adapting the kernel parameters using an online Bayesian optimization strategy. The core claim is that kernel learning algorithms can be effectively adapted to evolving data streams, leading to improved performance and reduced retraining frequency. The proposed method continuously updates the kernel function based on incoming data, leveraging the uncertainty estimates from Bayesian optimization to guide the adaptation process. This allows the algorithm to respond to changes in the data stream's distribution, maintaining accuracy over time. The key innovation lies in the seamless integration of a kernel learning algorithm with an online Bayesian optimization strategy, providing a robust and scalable solution for data stream mining scenarios where data is inherently non-stationary. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical analysis and outline the key components for implementation.

title: Causal Inference via Graph Laplacian Eigenmaps and Bayesian Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to causal inference that leverages the strengths of graph Laplacian eigenmaps and Bayesian networks. Traditional causal inference methods often rely on stringent assumptions regarding data distributions, which can be difficult to verify in practice. Our method addresses this challenge by first employing graph Laplacian eigenmaps to automatically identify nodes within a causal network that exhibit similar causal relationships. These identified nodes are then used to construct a Bayesian network, incorporating both the discovered relationships and prior domain knowledge. This framework offers a more flexible and robust approach to causal inference, particularly in scenarios where assumptions about data distributions are uncertain or incomplete. The core claim of this work is that strong distributional assumptions are often a barrier to effective causal inference, and our method offers a mechanism to overcome this limitation through network-based discovery and Bayesian modeling. We demonstrate the potential of this combined approach, focusing on the underlying mechanics and theoretical justification.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Computing Heterogeneity Optimization
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed computing heterogeneity optimization driven by quantum entanglement. Traditional distributed computing systems face significant challenges in efficiently utilizing diverse computing resources, leading to performance bottlenecks. We introduce a framework that leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to establish a quantum entanglement network, enabling high-fidelity, low-latency communication and computation across heterogeneous nodes. The core idea involves distributing computational tasks across these nodes based on their specific capabilities, utilizing entangled states to facilitate efficient data exchange and collaborative processing. The theoretical framework is presented, outlining the key mathematical concepts and optimization strategies. We demonstrate the potential of this approach to overcome the limitations of conventional methods and achieve significant improvements in distributed computing performance. The proposed system utilizes entanglement to achieve a level of computational coordination previously unattainable, offering a fundamentally new paradigm for distributed problem-solving. The focus here is on the theoretical foundations and potential benefits of the entanglement-based approach.

title: Zero-Point Field Bias Field Optimization
abstract: This paper explores a novel algorithmic framework for optimizing zero-point field biases in quantum systems, with the goal of enhancing coherence and entanglement generation. We introduce a "Feedback Loop Resonance" system – a dynamically adjusting field strength and phase – to continuously self-correct the bias based on observed quantum states. This approach leverages a fundamental physical phenomenon to achieve improved quantum performance. The core mechanism centers around constant adjustment, creating a self-correcting bias that significantly improves the quality of quantum states. We present a theoretical analysis and initial experimental validation demonstrating the effectiveness of this framework. This work offers a promising pathway for advancing quantum technologies.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Automated Theorem Proving
abstract: Automated theorem proving (ATP) systems have achieved significant progress in verifying logical statements, yet they often grapple with complex and incomplete proofs, frequently failing to provide solutions or generating lengthy, unproductive search paths. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging reinforcement learning (RL) to address these limitations. The core idea involves training an RL agent to guide the theorem proving process, effectively learning a heuristic function that prioritizes proof steps. The agent interacts with the ATP system, receiving rewards based on the advancement of the proof and penalties for unproductive steps. Through this iterative process, the agent learns to strategically navigate the proof space, optimizing the search for a valid conclusion. This approach offers a dynamic and adaptive method for theorem proving, potentially surpassing the constraints of static, hand-crafted heuristics and ultimately enhancing the efficiency and success rate of ATP systems. The method is presented with a detailed description of the agent architecture, reward function design, and training methodology.

title: Quantum-Inspired Bayesian Inference with Adaptive Superposition
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to Bayesian inference that draws inspiration from the principles of quantum mechanics, specifically superposition and measurement. Rather than implementing a full quantum computation, we introduce a classical "superposition layer" within the Bayesian inference process. This layer simultaneously represents multiple hypotheses as probabilistic superpositions, allowing for a potentially significant acceleration of the inference process. Adaptive measurement strategies are employed to dynamically collapse these superpositions, favoring the most probable solution based on evolving evidence. The core claim is that by mimicking the effects of quantum superposition, we can achieve substantial improvements in the speed and efficiency of Bayesian inference, particularly for complex problems where traditional methods may struggle. This work outlines the theoretical framework, describes the key components of the proposed system, and discusses the potential benefits and challenges of this quantum-inspired approach. We demonstrate that this method can effectively address challenges in areas such as parameter estimation, model selection, and decision-making under uncertainty. The adaptive nature of the measurement process is crucial for scaling this approach to larger and more intricate Bayesian models.

title: World Layer Model (WLM): Structural Prompt Conditioning with Increasing Advantage on Structurally Demanding Tasks and Superior Token Efficiency
abstract: We present the World Layer Model (WLM), a prompt architecture that fixes the structure of an answer before the model writes it. The prompt states what the answer must contain, how each claim's epistemic status must be marked, and which of four output templates applies, selected from the task's type by table lookup. We compare WLM against four baselines — no conditioning, a structured four-step protocol, chain-of-thought, and explicit uncertainty prompting — and against a structure-only variant of WLM itself. All conditions were run on 85 tasks spanning three difficulty tiers, from standard reasoning to adversarial epistemic traps and open-ended strategic problems, across six models from four vendors and two deployment modes, with every response scored by two independent LLM judges. WLM's advantage over the best baseline grows with the structural demands of the task, from +0.351 on the easiest tier to +1.197 on the hardest (5-point scale). Every other condition loses ground as the tasks get harder; WLM does not. It also produces the shortest responses of any condition, so the gain does not come at the cost of length. A supplementary comparison separates the two parts of the conditioning and finds they contribute in similar measure, with only the rules acting on the element set reducing output. The pattern holds for all six models and is largest for the smaller ones. On a knowledge-recall benchmark, where the answer depends on facts the prompt cannot supply, the accuracy advantage disappears while the epistemic-quality advantage does not.

title: Collaborative Weak-Supervision Annotation With Multiple Large Language Models and BERT for Hospital Patient Service Question Categorization: Development and Validation Study (Preprint)
abstract: BACKGROUND Hospital patient-service questions are short, colloquial messages in which one entry often bundles several requests with unclear business boundaries, making manual labeling costly. As internet hospitals and online patient-portal platforms scale, hospitals need automatic classification for triage, ticket routing, and risk detection. OBJECTIVE To develop and evaluate a multi–large language model (LLM) weak-supervision annotation pipeline combined with domain-adapted BERT (bert-base-chinese) fine-tuning that constructs a 20-category hospital patient-service label system and a binary outpatient-service classifier from routinely collected, de-identified consultations. METHODS We performed retrospective text mining on 145,128 de-identified consultations from a single tertiary internet hospital (de-identification GB/T 39725-2020; IRB approval 2026-E0760). Three LLMs (GLM, Qwen, LLaMA) independently labeled each text; full agreement was treated as a high-confidence signal and disagreement was routed to a fourth model (DeepSeek) and to human review. Twenty business labels were built through model proposal, semantic merging, and human revision. We fine-tuned bert-base-chinese for a binary outpatient-service task and a 20-class task, and evaluated accuracy, F1, AUC-ROC/AUC-PR, agreement (Fleiss Kappa, ICC), and a temporally held-out external-validation set of 4,135 later consultations. RESULTS Of 145,128 valid texts, 57.2% had full tri-model agreement (Fleiss Kappa 0.6205; ICC 0.6329). After review, 136,979 samples (94.4%) received labels. evidence.title: Collaborative Weak-Supervision Annotation With Multiple Large Language Models and BERT for Hospital Patient Service Question Categorization: Development and Validation Study (Preprint)
evidence.abstract: BACKGROUND Hospital patient-service questions are short, colloquial messages in which one entry often bundles several requests with unclear business boundaries, making manual labeling costly. As internet hospitals and online patient-portal platforms scale, hospitals need automatic classification for triage, ticket routing, and risk detection. OBJECTIVE To develop and evaluate a multi–large language model (LLM) weak-supervision annotation pipeline combined with domain-adapted BERT (bert-base-chinese) fine-tuning that constructs a 20-category hospital patient-service label system and a binary outpatient-service classifier from routinely collected, de-identified consultations. METHODS We performed retrospective text mining on 145,128 de-identified consultations from a single tertiary internet hospital (de-identification GB/T 39725-2020; IRB approval 2026-E0760). Three LLMs (GLM, Qwen, LLaMA) independently labeled each text; full agreement was treated as a high-confidence signal and disagreement was routed to a fourth model (DeepSeek) and to human review. title: Geometry Conditioning in an Embodied SLM: Training Controls and Robustness Diagnostics in a 0.8B Hybrid Model
abstract: We study how physical-state inputs affect a 0.8B hybrid language model adapted for manipulation with 6.2M trainable parameters. Six conditions are trained on three LIBERO-Spatial tasks and evaluated over three seeds and 540 held-out rollouts. Conditioning recurrent decay gates on geometric increments yields 28.9% success, compared with 36.7% when those increments are shuffled during training and 24.4% without explicit object/goal geometry. Both geometry policies receive correct inputs at evaluation. A token adapter using the same increments scores 27.8%; differences vary across seeds and remain inconclusive. Token-clock conditioning scores 11.1%, including one seed that fails to converge. In separate robustness tests, a state-only relative-coordinate policy retains 7/10 success under frame relabeling, whereas all four tested visual policies fall to at most 3/20 after a 5 cm object displacement. These results show no reliable advantage from training-time geometric alignment under this recipe and illustrate the gap between coordinate invariance and physical-layout generalization. Episode records, seed-level analyses, and figure-generation code accompany the paper.

title: DAIMO 0.1.7: Ontology and Reproducibility Package
abstract: DAIMO (Dataspace AI Model Ontology) is an ontology for representing metadata required to discover, execute and evaluate artificial intelligence models in governed data spaces. This deposit preserves the evaluated DAIMO 0.1.7 ontology and its reproducibility materials. The package distinguishes three sources: the ontology release evaluated at commit cd3c1ae0f8ad262fbbe899dd9b8b95db128becad; the regenerated documentation and technical evidence preserved at commit b355abcab259bc3609eb72317a63c8c90b8af92c; and the external OOPS! evaluation performed on 7 September 2026. The OOPS! scan examined only the DAIMO core and returned no critical pitfalls, two important findings associated with reused external vocabulary terms, and two minor findings. These results did not require changes to the native DAIMO ontology. The package includes ontology serializations, alignments, SHACL shapes, example data, competency questions, tests, validation evidence, generated documentation, provenance information and integrity manifests. No production deployment or operational integration in a data space is claimed.

title: Probability Group Theory Adaptive Optimization Algorithm Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic group theory-based adaptive optimization algorithm framework designed to handle complex environments and dynamic requirements. The framework dynamically adjusts optimization goals and parameters through the probabilistic evolution of a group, allowing the algorithm to adapt to evolving conditions. We demonstrate the framework's efficacy through a series of simulated scenarios, highlighting its robustness and adaptability compared to traditional optimization methods. The core mechanism centers around leveraging probabilistic group dynamics to capture and respond to environmental shifts, leading to improved performance in heterogeneous settings.

title: Adaptive Noise Shaping in Quantum Field Theory
abstract: This paper investigates the challenges and opportunities presented by quantum field theory simulations, particularly concerning the inherent noise present within the system. We propose a novel adaptive noise shaping mechanism utilizing a feedback loop to dynamically adjust noise parameters in response to simulation output, aiming to minimize errors and enhance the precision of quantum field calculations. The core claim is that this design will significantly improve the accuracy and reliability of simulations, addressing a critical limitation in current approaches. This work introduces a framework for automatically optimizing noise shaping based on simulation results, representing a fundamental shift in how we manage and mitigate noise in quantum field calculations.

title: Dynamic Topology Structures and Machine Learning Self-Adaptation Algorithms
abstract: Dynamic Topology Structures and Machine Learning Self-Adaptation Algorithms explores novel approaches to enhance learning efficiency and outcome quality through dynamic adaptation of topology and model parameters. This research introduces a framework that iteratively adjusts the underlying topology of a learning system based on the input data, optimizing the learning process. The core mechanism involves leveraging dynamic topology and a self-adaptive machine learning model, allowing the system to dynamically adjust its parameters to minimize error and maximize accuracy. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the framework's performance, demonstrating significant improvements in learning speed and generalization ability compared to traditional methods. The study highlights the potential of this approach to address challenges in machine learning, particularly in complex and dynamic environments.

title: Self-Adaptive Machine Learning for Non-Linear Model Prediction
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive machine learning framework for predictive modeling, focusing on the ability to dynamically adjust model parameters in response to data non-linearities. Traditional machine learning methods often rely on fixed, predetermined model parameters, which struggle to effectively handle complex, non-linear relationships within data. We propose a system that employs an adaptive adjustment mechanism, iteratively refining model parameters based on observed data patterns. This approach offers improved accuracy and generalization capabilities compared to static models. The core of our design is a feedback loop that continuously assesses model performance and adjusts parameters to minimize error, ultimately optimizing the predictive outcome. This work addresses a critical limitation in many predictive applications where data exhibits complex, non-linear dynamics.

title: tvbench: a caller-side benchmark for telephony voice agents
abstract: tvbench measures what a caller hears from a telephony voice agent rather than what the agent reports about itself. Acting as the Asterisk side of an AudioSocket connection, it timestamps every audio frame an agent returns and derives frame pacing, delivery burstiness, continuity within a turn, and barge-in cut latency. A reference agent with switchable defects (bursting, mid-turn stalls, ignoring an interrupting caller) provides a falsification pass, so every metric is demonstrated to move when the defect it targets is introduced. Published results include that validation matrix.

title: 基于图的动态概率模型
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic probabilistic model based on graph representations, designed to effectively model complex systems exhibiting intricate probability relationships. The core mechanism centers around dynamically adjusting graph structures to capture the system's evolving behavior. Traditional probabilistic models often lack the flexibility to adequately represent these dynamic relationships. This work presents a robust and adaptable framework that leverages graph theory to enhance the modeling of systems with significant uncertainty and emergent behavior. We demonstrate the model's effectiveness through illustrative examples and rigorous analysis, emphasizing its capacity to capture complex dependencies and predict system dynamics. The core claim is that this approach offers a significant advancement over existing probabilistic models by providing a dynamically responsive representation of probability, facilitating more accurate predictions and a deeper understanding of system behavior.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for dynamic adaptive variable space modeling, leveraging machine learning to automatically adjust variable distributions and parameters to enhance model prediction accuracy. The study emphasizes the benefits of automated optimization and its potential to revolutionize predictive modeling.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Quantum State Estimation for Large-Scale Data
abstract: Quantum state estimation is a crucial component of many quantum computing applications, particularly for analyzing large datasets. Current classical algorithms struggle to efficiently estimate the state of quantum systems, limiting the practical utility of quantum computation. This paper explores the implementation of a novel quantum-enhanced algorithm to address this challenge, aiming to significantly improve the accuracy and efficiency of state estimation for large-scale data. We detail the core mechanism of utilizing quantum phenomena to reduce computational complexity and explore potential advancements in this field. The study focuses on demonstrating the algorithm's effectiveness through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation, highlighting its potential to unlock new capabilities in quantum data analysis.

title: 基于拓扑的几何信息加密
abstract: This paper introduces a novel cryptographic system based on topological geometry, offering enhanced security and integrity compared to traditional cryptographic methods. The system leverages the inherent structure of geometric spaces to embed data within a secure and verifiable framework. We present a method for generating and analyzing topological invariants, which are then used to encrypt and decrypt data. The core principle is to create a 'fingerprint' of the data through its topological structure, allowing for efficient and secure verification. The proposed approach focuses on robustness against known attacks, emphasizing the mathematical rigor behind the encryption process. We detail the mathematical framework, the key generation process, and the encryption and decryption procedures. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential applications and future research directions.

title: Quantum State Collapse Optimization – A Dynamic Thresholding Strategy
abstract: Quantum state collapse represents a fundamental challenge in quantum information processing. Efficiently managing collapse rates is crucial for achieving desired outcomes, such as quantum computation and quantum sensing. This paper introduces a dynamic thresholding strategy for optimizing collapse rates, utilizing information theory and generative adversarial networks (GANs) to dynamically adjust parameters. The core mechanism centers on learning the optimal collapse parameters through a GAN-based training process, which focuses on maximizing fidelity while minimizing computational cost. We present a framework for implementing this strategy and demonstrate its effectiveness through theoretical analysis and preliminary simulations.
